title: Perplexity launches privacy-minded ‘hybrid compute’ AI feature for Mac
snippet: Aside from being featured by Apple in the M6 Mac mini launch, Perplexity has been relatively quiet on the Mac front this summer. That changes today with hybrid compute for Mac. more…
fullText:
Aside from being featured by Apple in the M6 Mac mini launch, Perplexity has been relatively quiet on the Mac front this summer. That changes today with hybrid compute for Mac.

Perplexity first announced work on splitting AI tasks between local and cloud models in June. Today, Hybrid Compute is launching as part of Perplexity’s Mac app.

“Computer now splits a task between cloud models and a local model on your Mac,” the company says.

“Computer starts each task in the cloud. Trigger one from your iPhone, and your Mac accesses your files and runs sensitive steps locally.”

Introducing hybrid compute in Perplexity Computer.

Computer can start a task in the cloud, then move to a local model that runs on your Mac. Use it for steps involving private files or sensitive data.

Available today in the Perplexity Mac app. pic.twitter.com/bafirGWgwA

— Perplexity (@perplexity_ai) September 1, 2026

Perplexity’s website explains how the new feature works:

Our on-device PII classifier reads each task on the Mac before it is sent. Names, addresses, and account numbers are swapped for stand-ins, then restored when the answer returns.

We’ve open-sourced the on-device PII classifier, trained in collaboration with Perplexity’s Secure Intelligence Institute.

Macs with 8GB and 16GB RAM won’t be able to run hybrid compute, according to Perplexity. 24GB memory is the minimum, and 32GB is recommended as the floor:

Hybrid Compute runs on Apple silicon, macOS 15+ — 24 GB unified memory minimum, 32 GB for best results. Set up the local model once: download PPLX Qwen 3.8 27B in one click. No Ollama or manual runtime setup. Work it handles uses no cloud credits. No API key.

MacStories also has coverage of the new Perplexity feature today. You can learn more from Perplexity’s announcement page here.

Hybrid compute is just the latest AI tool from Perplexity that takes advantage of the power of the Mac. In May, the company overhauled its Mac app with a whole new version. Apple specifically cites Perplexity Personal Computer as a productivity use case for the new M6 Mac mini as well.

title: Meta Ray-Ban update will block the most obvious loophole for disabling the privacy LED
snippet: Meta continues to crack down on malicious users disabling the privacy LED on its Ray-Ban smart glasses, this time focusing on the most obvious loophole out there. more…
fullText:
Meta continues to crack down on malicious users disabling the privacy LED on its Ray-Ban smart glasses, this time focusing on the most obvious loophole out there.

Detailed by Meta’s VP of AR, Alex Himel, on Threads, a new update is “coming” to Ray-Ban smart glasses and Meta Smart Glasses to further block users from disabling the privacy LED. 

Previously, Meta targeted users who were modifying the hardware to disable the LED, but it left the door open to an easier loophole – starting the recording and then covering the LED. While the glasses would block a recording from starting when the LED was covered, this loophole allowed users to cover the LED after the recording had already started. This new update stops the camera from recording if the light is covered.

Himel explains:

	

We have an update coming to increase the reliability of the capture LED on our AI glasses. The camera won’t start recording if the LED is blocked, but some people try to bypass this by starting a recording and then covering it up. A fix for this is starting to roll out – the camera will now stop working if the light is covered during a recording.

We’re going to keep rolling out updates like this to make sure the capture LED can reliably alert bystanders when photos or videos are being captured for someone’s gallery. Only a tiny minority of people try to get around these protections, and the fact they have to go to these lengths shows our efforts are working. We’ll keep improving and evolving our approach. 

On a dedicated privacy page on its website, Meta says that if the glasses “detect the Capture LED light was covered, physically tampered or destroyed, they’ll automatically disable the camera,” adding that “it’s that simple.” The page also goes over “tips to help you and those around you feel safe and comfortable while you’re wearing your glasses” such as turning off the glasses in “sensitive spaces” and reasoning that you shouldn’t record with glasses if you wouldn’t record with your phone. 

The page also, notably, points out that “You, and only you” can see photos and videos captured on the glasses. That’s seemingly contrary to past reports that human moderators see videos from the glasses. 

It’s unclear exactly when this next update will roll out, but it comes as smart glasses are under intense scrutiny from society, with Meta the main name in that conversation.

title: Nvidia is buying Hugging Face for almost $13 billion
snippet: Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, bringing one of the most popular hosting platforms for open-source AI models, datasets, and tools under the ownership of the world's biggest AI chipmaker. Hugging Face is an online platform founded in 2016 that gives AI developers a space to share their projects and data with other users and the general public. It's often described as the "GitHub" for AI due to its browsable library of open-source machine learning models and emphasis on community collaboration features. "Together, we will scale Hugging Face's platform, strengthen its infrastructure and expand access to AI for develo … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, bringing one of the most popular hosting platforms for open-source AI models, datasets, and tools under the ownership of the world’s biggest AI chipmaker.

Hugging Face is an online platform founded in 2016 that gives AI developers a space to share their projects and data with other users and the general public. It’s often described as the “GitHub” for AI due to its browsable library of open-source machine learning models and emphasis on community collaboration features.

“Together, we will scale Hugging Face’s platform, strengthen its infrastructure and expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in his announcement. “Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem. Developers will choose the models they want, the frameworks they want, the clouds and inference service providers they want and the computing platforms they want. Nvidia compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face.”

Speculation regarding a potential Hugging Face acquisition started on August 23rd, after Business Insider reported that the startup was working with a bank to explore options for a $13 billion sale. By August 27th, Business Insider reported that Nvidia had been having acquisition conversations with Hugging Face over the previous week, though an earlier report by The Information said that a $12.9 billion deal between the companies had already been agreed upon.

While these reports couldn’t be independently verified at the time, Nvidia has now publicly declared its intentions to purchase the open-source AI repository. With open-source developers currently racing to catch up with closed AI systems, Nvidia stands to gain a strategic foothold to help preserve its AI hardware dominance now that closed-source AI providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are attempting to produce their own AI chips.

The last official valuation Hugging Face had was $4.5 billion, off the back of a funding round in 2023 that Nvidia participated in. The Financial Times previously reported that Hugging Face rejected a $500 million investment offer from Nvidia last year that would have valued it at $7 billion, apparently expressing concerns over having a single, dominant investor.

The startup isn’t a significant money-maker, however. The Information reports that Hugging Face has recently been generating around $150 million in annualized revenue, barely a fraction of its purchase price. That said, as the world’s most valuable public company, Nvidia sure has a lot of money to throw around right now, and it seems happy to do so to protect the AI empire it’s been building.

title: Uber and Wayve Launch London’s First Public Robotaxi Service
snippet: The rides will take place in the Ford Mustang Mach-E. Initially, a safety operator will remain in the driver’s seat.
fullText:
London’s first public robotaxi service is now live. Starting today, UK riders can hail a self-driving vehicle via the Uber app, through a partnership with autonomous driving company Wayve – though a safety operator will initially remain in the driver’s seat.

At launch, the rides will take place aboard the all-electric Ford Mustang Mach-E. The vehicles are outfitted with cameras and radar, allowing Wayve’s AI Driver to navigate with “full 360-degree visibility around the car at all times,” the companies said in a press release. 

Eventually, rides can expand to other vehicles equipped with Wayve’s driverless tech. In fact, Wayve and Uber plan to open up self-driving trips aboard the Nissan Leaf in Tokyo later this year.

Wayve is one of a handful of autonomous vehicle (AV) companies looking to revolutionize urban transportation around the world. Competitors include Waymo, Zoox, Nuro, Avride and May Mobility – which all have partnerships with either Lyft, Uber or both. Waymo aims to launch its robotaxi service in London sometime this year, pending regulatory approval.

Unlike AV systems that rely on high-definition maps and hand-coded rules for perception and navigation, Wayve says it uses foundational AI models that allow its AI Driver to learn from real-world environments and then apply those driving skills “to unexpected scenarios, even without prior training exposure.” That means the tech can “adapt to new roads, vehicles, weather conditions and cities with unprecedented speed and efficiency,” according to the company.

The launch of the robotaxi service comes as Uber on Wednesday said it’s laying off around 10% of its staff. The cuts involve “simplifying team structures” by eliminating several management roles, CEO Dara Khosrowshahi noted in a message to employees, which the company later shared in a newsroom post. Uber plans to invest more in ride-hailing, delivery and robotaxi operations.

The Mach-E robotaxi is equipped with cameras and radar, allowing Wayve’s AI Driver to navigate with “full 360-degree visibility around the car at all times,” Uber and Wayve said.Uber/Wayve

Navigating the challenges ahead

Wayve was founded in 2017, and began operating on London’s public roads in 2020. That’s around the time Uber abandoned its own self-driving ambitions, opting to instead team up with more established players in the space.

In 2024, Uber and Wayve announced their collaboration, agreeing to bring Wayve-powered vehicles to the Uber network. That was followed by plans the following year to launch self-driving trials on public streets in London.

As driverless cars expand into more cities, they face a unique set of challenges shaped by distinct local cultures, roads and regulations. London may prove especially challenging, with its narrow, one-way routes and free-wheeling (and assertive) pedestrians. Additionally, the city’s iconic black-cab culture has endured even as ride-hailing apps transformed how people get around. Now, autonomous vehicles could trigger another seismic shift in the city’s transportation landscape – and potentially provoke fierce resistance from an industry that’s already weathered one tech-fueled wave of disruption.

At launch, Wayve will manage its fleet, while Otto Car, which provides private car rental services, will oversee the trained onboard safety drivers. Uber will eventually take over day-to-day fleet operations alongside Otto Car. The two companies will run a depot in London, which will serve as a hub for everything from vehicle maintenance to servicing and charging. There will also be charging pitstops throughout the operating area to boost vehicle uptime (and maximize profits).  

From the start, Uber will handle rider support, while Wayve will oversee its driverless tech. 

“We’re proud to introduce the Wayve AI Driver to the public for the first time right here in London, our home city and one of the most complex driving environments in the world,” Alex Kendall, CEO and co-founder of Wayve, said in a statement. “Autonomous driving technology will complement the city’s rich transport network, and we’re excited for Londoners to experience it first as we begin our global rollout with Uber.” 

Riders will be notified when they’re matched with a robotaxi in the Uber app, and have the option to accept or select a standard ride instead.Uber/Wayve

How to hail a Wayve robotaxi ride on Uber

Starting today, if you request an UberX, Uber Comfort or Uber Electric ride in London, you could be matched with a Wayve-powered Mach-E vehicle. There is no additional cost and you’ll see the pricing up front. 

The vehicles will drive autonomously, though initially, a safety operator will oversee the trip and offer support or take the wheel if needed. “This is part of our phased introduction, before fully driverless operations begin in the future,” Uber and Wayve said in a release. 

Riders will get a notification each time they’re matched with an AV, with the option to accept the ride or switch to a non-autonomous vehicle. So if you’re not thrilled about having an AI-powered driver, you won’t be forced to take one of these vehicles.

On the flip side, if you’re eager to get in an AV, you can boost your chances of being matched with one by opting in via the Uber app. Go to Account > Settings > Autonomous Vehicles (under Ride Preferences) and hit the toggle next to “Get more autonomous rides.”

Once the car arrives, you can unlock it and begin the trip from the Uber app. There’s also a touchscreen in the vehicle for starting the ride and seeing the planned route – similar to what you’ll find in other self-driving vehicles from companies like Waymo. Riders can access human support in the Uber app, or from the safety operator in the vehicle. 

You’ll be able to rate the trip afterward, but won’t be prompted to tip.

title: India’s richest man now wants to turn aging computers into AI-ready PCs
snippet: Jio is betting it can turn an aging computer into an AI-ready PC for as little as about $11 for two months.
fullText:
Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Jio is opening its cloud PC service to any internet user in India, positioning it as a way to turn aging computers into AI-ready machines without hardware upgrades.

On Wednesday, Reliance Jio expanded JioPC, originally launched in July 2025, beyond its own broadband subscribers, making the service available as a stand-alone subscription to users with an internet connection, regardless of their telecom or broadband provider. The service streams a virtual PC from Jio’s cloud to an existing computer, with plans offering up to eight virtual CPUs, 16GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage.

Jio says the service can give even computers as old as eight years access to the computing power needed for modern AI applications, without users replacing their machines or installing new hardware. Plans start at ₹1,000 (about $11) for two months, while a 12-month subscription costs ₹4,000 (around $42) for 8GB of RAM and 500GB of storage, or ₹5,000 (about $53) for the 16GB and 1TB configuration.

India had more than 65 million PCs in use in 2025, including about 34 million consumer and 31 million commercial machines, according to estimates from IDC, which expects the installed base to approach 69 million by the end of 2026.

Ambani’s move comes amid widening replacement cycles. Consumers and small businesses in India typically replace their PCs every five to six years, compared with four to five years in 2022, IDC’s senior market analyst Bharath Shenoy told TechCrunch. Enterprises are stretching their machines for longer too, with replacement cycles reaching about four years, up from three previously.

Jio is betting that cloud computing can stretch those lifecycles further. By shifting much of the processing and storage away from the device and into its data centers, India’s most valuable company can keep adding computing capacity without requiring users to replace the machines sitting on their desks.

Prabhu Ram, vice president of the industry research group at the Gurugram-based market analyst firm CyberMedia Research, said JioPC could instead create a market where consumers pay for computing capability rather than repeatedly spending on hardware upgrades.

“Jio is broadening its value proposition by opening JioPC to non-Jio users, while also challenging the traditional hardware upgrade cycle,” Ram told TechCrunch.

However, he does not expect that model to replace conventional PCs. JioPC, he noted, could create a parallel, price-sensitive tier for households, students, and others “for whom buying a new AI-capable PC was never really on the table to begin with.”

Indians have traditionally preferred owning their hardware over paying for PCs as a service, Shenoy said. Jio will have to convince consumers that a recurring subscription is worth giving up some of the advantages of a conventional PC, including the ability to keep working without the internet.

That dependence could be particularly prominent in the smaller cities and towns where affordable computing has the most room to grow. JioPC requires a stable internet connection, and any disruption can affect the user experience, unlike a conventional computer.

Additionally, there is competition at the low end from refurbished PCs, which Shenoy said allow consumers to own inexpensive hardware without remaining dependent on connectivity.

Jio’s pitch of an “AI-ready” PC through JioPC also challenges the conventional idea of what an AI PC looks like. The company has not disclosed much about the underlying hardware powering the cloud service. However, the specifications it has provided do not mention dedicated AI accelerators for on-device generative AI workloads, which is a key feature of the new generation of AI PCs.

Moreover, the real test for Jio, Ram said, is whether people come to see cloud computing as a “daily utility” rather than an “opportunistic workaround,” and are willing to pay for computing power instead of buying new hardware.

title: HiddenLayer nabs $100M as enterprises rush to secure their AI deployments
snippet: Security companies are scrambling to build products that can monitor not just agents but also the tools and add-ons they use.
fullText:
When AI security startup HiddenLayer raised its $50 million Series A three years ago, one of the big questions in the space was whether the AI threats the startup was protecting against would manifest in enough quantity to make for a real market. As my former colleague Kyle Wiggers noted at the time, it was difficult to pin down real examples of attacks against AI at scale.

How quickly things have changed. Security companies are now scrambling to build products that can monitor not just agents but also the tools and add-ons they use. While there still aren’t many headlines about agents being exploited, the risk of agents going haywire during production is nevertheless real. And so the market for tools to prevent that from happening has exploded: Gartner estimates companies will spend $2.83 billion this year on products meant to secure AI tools, 83% more than 2025, and expects spending to reach nearly $4.78 billion next year.

HiddenLayer, which makes tools to protect AI models, agents, and workflows from adversarial attacks, vulnerabilities, and malicious code injections, has been able to take good advantage of that shift. Its co-founder and CEO, Chris Sestito, tells TechCrunch that the startup’s annual recurring revenue grew more than 10x over the past year. He declined to give an exact number but said ARR is now in the “tens of millions” of dollars, and over 90% of that growth was driven by new customers signing in the past year.

Financial services and large tech companies building AI products are currently the company’s largest verticals, and it also has contracts with the Department of Defense and intelligence community. One of its customers is apparently a “leading frontier model provider” with “more than 700 million weekly users,” which sounds like OpenAI or Anthropic to me.

To make the most of that momentum, the startup has now raised $100 million in a Series B funding round that was led by Delta-v Capital, with participation from Ten Eleven Ventures, Morgan Stanley, Microsoft’s M12, Booz Allen Hamilton, and others. 

The Austin-based startup broadly still sells what it used to in 2023, but Sestito told TechCrunch that the biggest change it’s had to make was to extend its existing products — discovery, runtime protection, attack simulation, and supply chain security — to address prompt injection, agent manipulation, and malicious tool use.

“Inference is still inference. So whether it’s on a traditional machine learning model, whether it’s GenAI, whether it’s an agentic work stream, a lot of our technology still applied. So really, we haven’t had to pivot, but we’ve had to grow our scope … from traditional modeling to GenAI to agentic,” he said.

Sestito stressed that runtime security has especially become a priority as AI deployments grow common across businesses and likened it to traditional endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions, but specifically for AI.

The company’s new products reflect that shift, and Sestito highlighted a new opportunity for attackers in exploiting open source models. “We parse and scan about 50 different AI file frameworks to make sure that, especially in the case of open source, open-weight models, that the tool you’re working with is the one you believe it to be, and it’s the one it’s purporting to be. We’re looking at things like models purporting to be one thing, but they’re another — hidden models inside of models,” he said.

The startup says the new $100 million is going to help it build in that direction, though with more of a focus on sales and distribution, while continuing to expand its engineering and research. It also plans to expand into Europe and EMEA.

HiddenLayer may find itself tapping that war chest for more, though. Large cybersecurity companies, like Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, and Check Point often prefer to buy rather than build this sort of tech, while startups like Noma and Zenity have raised over $100 million each to take on adjacent or overlapping areas of this space.

Sestito acknowledged that some parts of the AI security products his company offers could eventually be bundled into the platforms built by companies such as Microsoft, OpenAI, and AWS. However, he expects AI infrastructure will grow toward governance features such as discovery, identity, and policy controls, rather than the kind of tools that his company builds.

For now, he says HiddenLayer’s job is to “scale vertically alongside artificial intelligence,” and eventually expand horizontally into parts of cybersecurity that increasingly depend on AI. That’s an ambitious goal, but the startup first has to prove it can turn its head start into an enduring business before the rest of the industry catches up.

title: Apple will be launching its first pair of smart glasses next year: Here’s what’s coming
snippet: As soon as next year, Apple will be debuting its first pair of AI-powered smart glasses. They’ll integrate Visual Intelligence and bring Siri to the real world. Here’s what we’re expecting. more…
fullText:
As soon as next year, Apple will be debuting its first pair of AI-powered smart glasses. They’ll integrate Visual Intelligence and bring Siri to the real world. Here’s what we’re expecting.

Core features

First and foremost, these glasses are AI glasses, not AR glasses. That means they’ll primarily be voice and camera-based, as they won’t have any displays.

The cameras will allow Siri to look at your real world environment and answer questions, provide context, and translate signage. Another feature that we’ll likely see on these glasses is the ability for you to ask Siri to save an image of something and remind you later, as we first saw in the macOS 26.7 leak.

They’ll also offer speakers for music and audio playback, so you can think of them as open-ear headphones.

On the other hand, though – they might not allow for the glasses to take photos and videos normally, per Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. Meta’s Ray-Ban glasses have become a massive privacy concern lately, and Apple may want to avoid that.

Styles

Unlike Meta, Apple isn’t partnering with an existing eyewear-maker to design these glasses. According to Bloomberg, the company is instead designing them in house, with a number of different styles in the works:

A large rectangular frame, reminiscent of Ray-Ban Wayfarers

A slimmer rectangular design, similar to the glasses worn by Apple Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook

Larger oval or circular frames

A smaller, more refined oval or circular option

They’re supposedly going to be made of acetate, a more durable and higher-end alternative to plastic. Apple will also offer them in a few finishes, including black, ocean blue, and light brown.

Health

In a future iteration of the product, Apple is reportedly considering positioning the product as a health device. This could mean they’ll integrate heart-rate monitors (similar to AirPods Pro 3), and it could mean there’ll be additional software features (like Workout Buddy from Apple Watch) to make it more helpful.

Beyond that, it’s unclear how Apple will make these useful for health – just don’t expect it in the first iteration.

Release date

	

Recent reporting suggests that Apple will unveil these glasses at WWDC 2027 to allow developers to prepare for them. Then, they’ll ship later that year. In all likelihood that’ll mean a September debut, alongside the 20th anniversary all-glass iPhone. You can learn more about that here.

title: Palo Alto Networks paid $500M for Thrive-backed Console, sources say
snippet: The acquisition also leaves Sequoia-backed Serval as the de facto startup leader in AI IT service automation, industry watchers believe.
fullText:
Palo Alto Networks paid $500 million in cash and stock to acquire Console, a two-year-old startup that uses AI agents to automate routine IT help desk tasks, according to two people with knowledge of the deal.

The companies officially announced the acquisition on Tuesday but didn’t reveal terms of the deal. Since its founding in 2024, Console has raised $29 million across two rounds: a $6.2 million seed led by Thrive Capital and a $23 million Series A co-led by DST Global and Thrive.

Before the sale, Console was valued at $157 million, according to PitchBook, delivering a rapid return for investors including SV Angel, Abstract Ventures, and notably Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora, who participated as an angel investor. Palo Alto Networks declined to comment.

The cybersecurity giant said that it will integrate Console into Cortex, its platform that uses AI to automatically detect and neutralize threats. Console’s agentic functionality will allow security teams to investigate and resolve alerts using natural language, giving Cortex “the arms and legs to deliver autonomous security outcomes across the entire enterprise,” as Arora described in a statement.

Console was founded by Andrei Serban, coming shortly after his previous startup — code-security platform Fuzzbuzz — was acquired by Rippling. The startup, whose customers included Ramp, Flock Safety, and Scale AI, automated tasks like password resets, granted access to apps like Figma and Miro, and performed routine troubleshooting without direct human involvement.

As a startup, Console competed primarily with Serval, another ServiceNow challenger that hit a $1 billion valuation after raising a $75 million Series B round led by Sequoia last December. Serval started as an AI tech support tool and quickly expanded to provide AI assistance for human resources, legal, and finance departments. Console’s acquisition leaves Serval as the category-leader-to-watch among startups automating IT service management, one investor, who is not a backer of Serval, told TechCrunch.

Console is Palo Alto Networks’ seventh acquisition in 2026, according to PitchBook. Other VC-backed companies scooped up by the cybersecurity behemoth this year include Greylock and Lux Capital-backed observability platform Chronosphere, at a valuation of $3.35 billion, and Koi, a cyber startup backed by Battery and Team8, for $400 million.

title: Adobe acquires Indian market intelligence startup Rilo
snippet: This is Adobe's second acquisition out of India after Rephrase.ai in 2023
fullText:
Adobe has acquired India-based marketing intelligence startup Rilo in a deal involving licensing and team acquisition, TechCrunch learned and the company confirmed. This is Adobe’s second acquisition from India after it bought video platform Rephrase.ai in 2023. The companies didn’t disclose the deal’s terms.

Beyond confirming the deal, Adobe declined to comment.

The acquisition gives Adobe a small team and technology focused on automating marketing workflows, which have been changing as companies use AI to build tools to automate the creation, deployment, and tracking of campaigns, get action items from meetings or calls to complete tasks, and increase brand visibility on platforms like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. Rilo’s technology could bolster Adobe’s existing products as the company targets its larger customers. 

Founded by IIT batchmates Georgi Boby and Dhruv Jaglan in 2025, Rilo raised $1 million from investors including Peak XV, DeVC, and Day Zero Ventures at a $10 million valuation. A source told TechCrunch that investors will get an exit from this deal, and Adobe will integrate some of Rilo’s IP along with the six-member team. Jaglan mentioned on LinkedIn that more than 10,000 people had tried out the tool.

The company worked on letting go-to-market teams create custom workflows, including competitor intelligence, content repurposing and distribution, and sales call analysis. It also allowed teams to set up custom workflows comparable to tools like Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work. 

Post-acquisition, Rilo will shut down and won’t be available to its customers.

Rilo co-founders Dhruv Jaglan and Georgi BobyImage Credits:Rilo

“We’re very excited that Rilo has been acquired by Adobe in such a short span of time,” Rahul Gupta, managing partner, Day Zero Ventures told TechCrunch over email. “Their workflow builder product was way ahead of the curve and shall be extremely valuable to a giant like Adobe in enhancing customer experience and productivity.”

Adobe made a marquee marketing acquisition last year by buying SEO optimization company Semrush for $1.9 billion. 

DeVC’s Rahul Mathur told TechCrunch that Rilo could fit into Adobe’s CX and marketing suite to handle complex workflows and give customers visibility into actions they take on the creative company’s platform. 

Rivals like Canva have also bolstered their marketing portfolio with acquisitions and new launches. Meanwhile, Amazon, Google, and Meta have built their own AI-powered marketing rails. 

The story has been updated with co-founders’ post mentioning the stat.

fullText:
Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

Belkin is joining companies like BMX, Kuxiu, and Zens with the launch of its first power banks featuring semi-solid-state battery technology. The company claims the new accessories have been “engineered to last up to 3x longer than other power banks” with the addition of a “gel-like layer” alongside the liquid electrolyte typically found in lithium-ion batteries.

Other advantages of what Belkin is calling its BoostSolid Cell technology include a reduced risk of overheating that could cause swelling or fires and consistent power delivery across a wider temperature range. They’re more expensive than power banks with comparable specs, but a longer functional lifespan should outweigh the premium pricing.

The UltraCharge Pro Slim Magnetic Power Bank 5K Qi2 15W with BoostSolid Cell is the smaller and cheaper option of Belkin’s two new power banks at $69.99. The company claims it’s 40 percent slimmer than other 5,000mAh power banks and is designed to magnetically hang on the back of compatible mobile devices and wirelessly deliver up to 15W of power. A USB-C charging port can also be used to power other devices at up to 22.5W, but charging two devices simultaneously drops the output to just 5W wirelessly and 12W with a USB-C cable.

The larger UltraCharge Pro Power Bank 10K 60W with BoostSolid Cell and Display offers twice the capacity with a 10,000mAh battery for an extra $20. The $89.99 power bank is also slimmer than competing options with similar capacities thanks to the increased energy density of its semi-solid-state battery tech. Power output maxes out at up to 60W when charging a single device over USB-C, but that drops when up to three devices are connected and charging using a pair of USB-C ports and a single USB-A port. And because putting screens on batteries is now en vogue, this one has a display showing charge level, power output, and the internal temperature.

title: Norway considers ban on camera-enabled wearable ‘pervert glasses’
snippet: The Nordic country says wearable camera headsets need to be regulated given their privacy risks.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

6:11 AM PDT · September 2, 2026

Image Credits:David Paul Morris / Bloomberg

		

							

											
									

					

	

Norway is considering a ban on smart glasses and other camera-enabled wearable headsets as it seeks to regulate the controversial technology amid privacy concerns.

The country’s digital minister Karianne Tung, as quoted by the AFP news agency, said that the government is looking to regulate the use of camera-enabled wearables, such as those made by Meta and Snap. These wearables feature cameras, are internet-connected, and may soon include facial recognition, drawing ire from civil liberties advocates, who say the devices intrude on people’s privacy. Some call the devices “pervert glasses,” prompting considerable consumer backlash.

Norway’s Tung said there is a “clear trend toward combining artificial intelligence with cameras and microphones built into glasses, headphones, hats and other objects we use in everyday life.”

“We must prevent this equipment from being used to monitor other people in public places,” said Tung, who added that this may include banning the use of facial recognition of other people in public places.

Tung plans to set up a group of experts to advise the government on better protecting people’s privacy rights.

title: It sure looks like hackers breached a major ID card verification service
snippet: An identity theft search site claimed to have more than 150 million driver's license photos stolen from an ID verification service. The crime site has now shut down.
fullText:
If you have handed over your driver’s license, passport, or other form of identity document to verify your information in the real world, like at a bar, a weed store, or when booking a car rental, there’s a good chance it’s now been stolen in a suspected massive data breach.

That’s according to a jaw-dropping report by independent security journalist Brian Krebs, who says a company used to verify government-issued identity documents in the real world was likely hacked and its vast stores of people’s ID cards were exfiltrated.

Krebs reports that an identity theft site called Nexus, which launched on the dark web this week, claimed to allow users to search through more than 150 million driver’s licenses and passports belonging to people who live in the United States and Canada. A post advertising the site on a known Russian cybercrime forum said Nexus added about half a million new documents daily, sourced from a “major identity verification company,” implying that the hackers had near real-time access to the identity verification company’s systems.

The advert claims that “customer photos are displayed if available.” Krebs found that his own driver’s license was among the searchable records in the database, confirming that the data was authentic. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth was also among the people whose photos were listed on the identity search site.

A spokesperson for the Department of Defense told TechCrunch that it is “aware of these reports and is evaluating them.”

Working with security researcher Zach Edwards, whose ID card was also stolen in the breach, Krebs identified the likely source as the identity verification service IDScan. The Louisiana-based company is relied on by major tech and consumer brands to verify tens of millions of people’s IDs around the world each month.

IDScan chief executive Jimmy Roussel did not return TechCrunch’s request for comment, but the company’s chief operating officer Jillian Kossman told Krebs that the company was investigating. Krebs said the FBI’s field office in New Orleans is also probing the breach. 

A spokesperson for the FBI confirmed that the bureau is “looking into the incident,” but declined to comment further.

Nexus went offline shortly after Krebs’ report went live.

This data breach comes as governments are increasingly rolling out age-verification laws, which largely rely on requiring adults to upload their identity documents to verify that they are old enough to enter a website or app. Security experts and privacy advocates have long warned that companies storing vast amounts of people’s identity documents for long periods of time put that data at risk of theft by hackers.

By all accounts, this would be the largest known single breach of identity documents in some time.

Updated with response from FBI.

The internet has a trust problem, and it’s not just because social media feeds are filling up with AI slop. AI-generated text and images are now making their way into job applications, product reviews, and even insurance claims, leaving platforms and users alike scrambling to figure out what’s real. 

A handful of startups have cropped up in the past couple of years to become the “trust layer” the internet needs — including Pangram. Watch as Pangram co-founder and CEO Max Spero joins TechCrunch’s Equity podcast to dig into the promise of AI detection tools and where to draw the line between AI assisted and AI generated.

title: Belkin says its new ‘BoostSolid’ Qi2 batteries last 3x longer than your other magnetic power banks
snippet: During IFA 2026, Belkin announced a new lineup of magnetic Qi2 battery banks using a new solid-state technology. The two UltraCharge Pro models can charge devices at up to 15W wirelessly, but they have more tricks in the sleeve. more…
fullText:
During IFA 2026, Belkin announced a new lineup of magnetic Qi2 battery banks using a new solid-state technology. The two UltraCharge Pro models can charge devices at up to 15W wirelessly, but they have more tricks in the sleeve.

It’s a little difficult to find good magnetic batteries that offer a reliable experience. The Qi2 standard isn’t exactly new, but plenty of batteries that snap to the back of your phone might not be capable of reaching 15W.

Belkin announced two new magnetic Qi2 batteries. They follow a common split into a 5,000mAh and a 10,000mAh power bank. Belkin says both UltraCharge Pro batteries are built on what it’s calling “BoostSolid” technology using internal gel layers for better performance, which it’s advertising lasts up to three times longer than other power banks.

That estimate comes from its ability to retain 80% capacity after 1,000 charge cycles. That’s a five-year lifespan on a full charge cycle every two days.

	

UltraCharge Pro Slim 5K
UltraCharge Pro 10K

The UltraCharge Pro Slim battery is the most pocket-friendly. It takes up little extra bulk compared to the larger model, but it only provides 5,000mAh of power. The thicker version has twice the capacity and adds a display for real-time battery status and alerts.

Both are certified for Qi2 15W wireless charging, but the UltraCharge Pro 10K is able to reach 60W wired charging from a single port, which opens it up to charge larger devices.

If you need something that will charge a laptop or gaming handhelds, the 10,000mAh UltraCharge Pro is likely the better bet. The Slim version is just as useful if space is a heavy consideration.

Belkin’s UltraCharge Pro Slim 5K and UltraCharge Pro 10K Qi2 batteries will be available starting this month from retailers like Amazon and Belkin’s website.

title: PSA: Amazon’s shopping AI can now tell you if that message is a scam
snippet: Amazon is adding a scam-detection feature to Alexa for Shopping that can verify whether suspicious emails, texts, and other messages actually came from the retailer.
fullText:
Amazon is turning to AI to help fight scammers, the company announced on Wednesday. The retailer said some 360,000 customers every year reach out to its customer service department wondering whether a message they received from Amazon is real or a scam. Now, customers will be able to ask Amazon’s consumer AI service, Alexa for Shopping, to help answer that question instead.

The company said its AI can “definitively” confirm whether a communication originated from its own systems by checking it against the billions of messages Amazon has sent globally. The AI analyzes the sender information, content, timing, message metadata, and more, to determine authenticity. Amazon said the system will improve as customers report more suspicious messages, helping it to spot scams more effectively in the future.

The new AI capabilities follow on Amazon’s earlier attempts to address the growing scam problem, which includes fake order confirmations, Prime membership renewal alerts, account suspension warnings, package delivery notifications, and job scams.

Earlier this year, Amazon launched an email address, verify@amazon.com, that allows anyone to forward suspicious messages to the company and receive a response that confirms whether the email was a real message or a scam. It also offers an online form on its customer service site that provides the same assistance.

The feature’s addition is another example of how Amazon has shifted its product strategy around Alexa to focus more on how it can assist with shopping-related questions and provide proactive help. Today, the assistant can source personalized deals, create shopping guides, help customers reorder their everyday items, offer AI product overviews, transcribe handwritten shopping lists, and more.

On Tuesday, the retailer also added an Alexa feature that lets customers set alerts when something new or relevant happens, like a favorite brand launching a new product, the release of a new book from a favorite author, or an artist dropping a new record.

Alexa for Shopping is available from both the Amazon website and mobile app.

title: Google AI Mode adds flight price tracking, hotel booking, & more travel tools
snippet: Google is rolling out a trio of updates that boost AI Mode’s travel capabilities, starting with the ability to get price alerts for flights. more…
fullText:
Google is rolling out a trio of updates that boost AI Mode’s travel capabilities, starting with the ability to get price alerts for flights.

Google Flights price tracking is coming directly into AI Mode. This integration starts with the ability to “describe where and when you want to fly.” You’ll see a list of flights and prices from “more than 300 partner airlines and travel sites.”

If you’re ready to book, you can build your full itinerary in AI Mode and buy your tickets through the airline’s website or your preferred booking platform.

Otherwise, you can follow up with “track these flight prices for me.” AI Mode will have you confirm the route, dates, and filters. Price changes will be delivered via email. Flight price tracking in AI Mode is now rolled out in over 180 countries/territories.

AI Mode can now show the cost of flights and hotels in points or miles. At launch, this feature supports Alaska Airlines / Hawaiian Airlines, American Airlines, Choice Hotels International, Hilton, and Wyndham Hotels & Resorts. Support for Accor, Flying Blue, Hyatt, LATAM Airlines, and Lufthansa Group will be available in the coming weeks.

	

This lets you ask: “I want to travel from Atlanta to Miami using my AA miles. Help me find some options for nonstop flights departing Oct 9 and returning on Oct 12.”

…you’ll see how many miles you need to book matching flights, based on the latest data directly from our partners.

The final travel update for AI Mode is hotel booking. This lets you chat about your preferences to get a list of hotels “complete with guest reviews and key factors to compare.” Once found, “Continue on Google” will appear for supported partners. 

From there, it’s just a few taps to pick your room type, review details like the cancellation policy, and complete the booking securely via Google Pay. When you book hotels through AI Mode, the hotel or booking platform will act as the merchant of record and handle any customer service.

This is rolling out now in the US with support for Booking.com, Choice Hotels International, Expedia, Hilton, Hotels.com, IHG Hotels & Resorts, Marriott International, Priceline, Trip.com, and Wyndham Hotels & Resorts.

In what could be fortuitous timing for hearing aid users, Anker announced its first over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids at IFA 2026. It was only a couple months ago when LXE Hearing, the parent company for Eargo and Lexie Hearing — two major OTC manufacturers in the US — decided to end US operations and exit the OTC hearing aid market. Now perhaps Anker can fill that void.

The receiver-in-canal (RIC) design has a main body that rests behind the ear. It uses Anker’s Thus chip, announced in April and first released in the Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro earbuds series. The chip delivers the best voice isolation I’ve ever heard on any audio product and could be an incredible boon for the hearing aids.

Anker’s RIC hearing aids use four beam-forming microphones to focus on who the user is speaking to in front of them. They get up to 12 hours of use (up to 36 hours with the case) and gain two hours of use with a five-minute fast charge — Anker claims this is the quickest fast charge among its competitors.

There aren’t any additional details about exact models or US availability and pricing, but we should know more by the end of the year.

title: Govee’s new ceiling light and LED strips are mood boosters with some AI sprinkled in
snippet: Govee launched a handful of new lighting options at IFA 2026, ranging from another ceiling light that responds to daylight to COB LED strips that use prompts to generate your lighting conditions. more…
fullText:
Govee launched a handful of new lighting options at IFA 2026, ranging from another ceiling light that responds to daylight to COB LED strips that use prompts to generate your lighting conditions.

Govee has been pushing to become one of the biggest names in smart home lighting, competing with massive brands like Philips Hue, GE Cync, and more. It’s recently begun expanding into ceiling lights, with a release earlier in the year that hinged on creating “living art.”

The ceiling light collection is growing with Govee’s IFA releases. The new Govee Sky Ceiling Light is an “AI-powered mood-responsive” option, because this is 2026 and every device needs a little AI. Right?

Calling it an AI light does it a bit of a disservice, because it sounds like a genuinely cool concept. Govee is working around the comfort wavelengths using the “vitality spectrum technology.” In essence, the ceiling light produces wavelengths that make up for deficiencies in natural lighting. Govee says this helps users maintain alertness during darker days.

	

The Sky Ceiling Light has a color temperature range from 1,000K to 10,000K, reaching up to 7,000 lumens of white light. Users will get the most out of it by using the “DaySync” feature in the Govee app, which uses weather and time data to adjust comfortable lighting conditions.

The massive ceiling light comes at a cost of $399.

On the more vibrant side of things, the Govee COB Strip Light 2 Pro uses AI in a similar way. Users can write prompts to generate lighting conditions for their space. It’s all need-dependent, and the AI Lighting Bot 2.0 model will create light sequences for different scenarios.

COB lights produce flicker-free output, and the Strip Light 2 Pro has 1,344 LEDs per meter with a triple-layer groove design. Govee says this ensures flawless output in single-color and dynamic color modes. The color temperature range echoes that of the ceiling light at 1,000K to 10,000K, and it uses Govee’s LumiBlend+ color engine to produce accurate colors.

The Pro model is Govee’s flagship LED strip at $169 per 5m, but the COB Strip Light 2 will also be available at a more affordable $99.

Govee’s Sky Ceiling Light and Strip Light 2 Pro will be available starting today from it’s website and at retailers like Amazon.

title: Hate AI Data Centers? Big Tech’s New Ad Campaign Aims to Change Your Mind
snippet: A multimillion-dollar campaign is trying to reverse the trend of the public’s growing disdain for AI data centers.
fullText:
xAI's data center operation in Memphis, Tennessee.

																			Steve Jones/Southern Environmental Law Center
												
			
				

If you’re part of the growing majority of Americans who oppose AI data centers, the US government and Big Tech have a message for you: Get over it.

The backlash against these massive AI server farms — notorious for guzzling energy and water — has been countered in recent days by aggressive public statements by President Donald Trump. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that local communities that don’t want data centers will end up “backwards and poor.” He went on to liken opposition to data centers to killing the “Golden Goose,” implying that we’re all to blame for blocking economic growth. 

CNET

And billionaire tech leaders, who have been especially cozy with the current administration, are taking to the field with a massive advertising blitz to sway public opinion, especially as November’s midterm elections approach. A group called Build American AI, funded by the pro-AI political action committee Leading the Future, is launching a multimillion-dollar campaign to try to counter the tide and promote the construction of AI data centers. The campaign’s initial rollout targets key election battleground states, starting with Kansas, Ohio and Wisconsin.

Opposition to data centers isn’t just about residents facing spiking electricity and water bills, though that would certainly be reason enough after five years of steadily high inflation. There’s also an array of environmental and health concerns, as well as general ambivalence or hatred of AI technology. Grassroots efforts, such as a nationwide map of data centers and proposed projects launched by activist Erin Brockovich, have helped communities organize and stay informed, while several cities have approved bans or moratoriums on new data center projects.

The sentiment against data centers shifted so quickly and sharply this year that a newly published Annenberg Public Policy Center study finds that around two-thirds (61%) of US adults oppose new data center builds near them. And that negative sentiment is across party lines, shared by Democrats (69%), Republicans (54%) and independents (53%).

Could a powerful network of political action committees and a barrage of expensive digital ads sway public opinion? Marketing experts told CNET it’ll be incredibly difficult to put that genie back in the bottle.

The main challenge is that society is incredibly polarized on AI-related issues right now, said Ari Lightman, professor of digital media and marketing at Carnegie Mellon University’s Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy. Tech companies are “trying to create an argument that local communities are going to benefit from the data center,” but those communities are “saying, no, we don’t believe you.”

According to Lightman, campaigns that attempt to shift public opinion on data centers must build a strong case for local benefits — and especially overcome deep-seated skepticism toward tech companies and AI.

Big Tech’s backers

The Build American AI campaign is part of the super-PAC network Leading the Future, which is bankrolled and organized by a coalition of powerful Silicon Valley investors, tech executives and veteran political operatives. The PR strategy is pretty straightforward: Rebrand data centers so they’re no longer seen as local nuisances but vital economic lifelines.

Key backers include billionaire venture capitalists Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, as well as Greg Brockman, the president of OpenAI. According to filings, Build American AI initially raised $100 million just from those parties. Other financial backers include Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale, who has been a donor and supporter of Trump; AI search engine Perplexity and investor Ron Conway.

The ad campaign would be a major influx of money toward pro-data center messaging. Advertising insights company AdImpact told CNET that, after tracking about 15,000 broadcast airings of data center-related ads, total spend is just $7.6 million this year, and most of it is directed against data centers. 

About 73% of the spending is from Democratic candidates, said John Link, VP of data at the firm. Most of the ads go after data centers directly or link opponents to their development, often due to rising energy costs or environmental concerns, Link said.

Earlier this year, Wired reported that Build American AI used a “dark money” campaign to pay TikTok and Instagram influencers to promote scripted messaging to frame aggressive AI development as a critical US national security priority against China. The new campaign could also rely on similar tactics and talking points. 

Trump’s recent Truth Social post said: “China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement.”

Persuading is a long road

Build American AI seems poised to hypertarget its ad buys to local news websites, streaming platforms and social media feeds — that way, the campaign reaches nearby residents and zoning decision-makers. In late July, Build American AI previewed its advertising materials to potential vendors and political strategy firms. Internal documents revealed that the campaign’s main thrust will be to portray data centers as engines of economic growth and job creation.

Given the widespread distrust of Big Tech, the ads are likely to avoid mentioning specific companies like Amazon, Google or Microsoft. Another tactic would be to reframe data centers as critical national infrastructure, treating them like public highways, water systems or the electrical grid.

Marketing experts CNET spoke with stressed that for the pro-AI messaging to work, it will have to thread the needle by addressing local concerns like energy and water usage while extolling the benefits data centers bring, such as employment and improved technologies that make people’s lives easier. The employment claim, however, has been met with skepticism. Most jobs created by data centers are construction-related and not long-term positions.

The other central issues to address would be resources, pollution and the lack of transparency around data center projects. Elie Barreby, head of SEO and AI search at Adorama, said that messaging in favor of data centers may fly directly in the face of what people are actually experiencing, such as noise pollution or rising utility bills.

“Nobody can advertise their way out of a bad user experience,” Barreby said. Communities  are facing “too many real-world negatives to be fooled by any marketing campaign, no matter how good!”

There’s been a heated debate over how many jobs data centers create beyond their initial construction phase.

Stephen Shankland/CNET

According to said Joe Szynkowski, founder of PR company The UpWrite Group, “the only way a national campaign can bring down the temperature will be tying the benefits of data centers to the everyday life of people in the affected communities.”

Any PR or marketing campaign requires making people feel something positive, but Szynkowski said tech companies haven’t done a great job with that kind of messaging so far. 

Lightman said there’ll need to be grassroots campaigning and boots on the ground to answer questions and remain consistent. Word spreads fast online if a data center’s promises aren’t met or if incentives are being offered in one location, but not in another.

Lightman isn’t very optimistic that these campaigns will effectively connect with and convince people who already feel misled or skeptical about AI and data centers.

“I don’t think the folks that are building the data centers frankly have the capability and wherewithal to do that,” he said.

title: Google Pics is Workspace’s new ‘pro-level’ AI image creator & editor
snippet: Following the announcement at I/O 2026 in May, Google Pics is launching in general availability today. more…
fullText:
Following the announcement at I/O 2026 in May, Google Pics is launching in general availability today.

Google Pics, which comes after Google Vids, is “built natively into Google Workspace.” You can click on an image in Google Docs or Slides and access the Pics editor as an overlay to start editing. An update in the coming weeks will let you edit images uploaded to Google Drive.

You can also access the tool from pics.new:

Besides generating a new image (with multiple options offered), you can import files from your computer, Google Drive, or Google Photos to start editing.

	

Leveraging Nano Banana, Google Pics offers “precise, object-based image editing.” Tools let you: 

Select and edit individual objects within an image 

Edit, reformat, or even translate individual text elements 

Crop your image for web, social media, print, or digital

Upscale your image to 2K or 4K

Process multiple edits at once, and revert any unwanted changes easily

The object segmentation capability lets you isolate a specific part and leave other parts of the image untouched. After selecting, you just provide text comments with the ability to “execute multiple edits at once.” Similarly, you can edit text that appears in images without changing anything else, which also allows for translation. 

Pics eliminates the frustration of wrangling pixels and feeling like you need to be a graphic designer to deliver a great image.

Based on the same editor as other Workspace apps, you can invite others to collaborate and share images via a link. Enterprise use cases include:

Create and translate social, digital, and web assets for global markets

Bring product concepts to life by placing them into any background or context

Brainstorm print designs, event collateral, or branded merchandise

Develop flyers, business cards, and much more

Google AI Pro and Ultra personal plans

title: Here’s how Apple Watch Ultra 4 will differentiate itself from prior models
snippet: Apple Watch Ultra 4 is coming on September 9, here are the key ways it’s rumored to differentiate itself from prior models. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch Ultra 4 is coming on September 9, here are the key ways it’s rumored to differentiate itself from prior models.

‘Significant upgrade’ to health sensors

Digitimes has reported on multiple occasions that Apple Watch Ultra 4 will bring significant upgrades to internal sensors. It went as far as saying “the number of sensor components will double.”

Mark Gurman reported this week that “upgrades to fitness tracking” are coming. And there’s evidence that a new high blood pressure-related feature has been reviewed by the FDA for release soon.

Though many specific details around these sensor additions are still unknown, it sounds like Apple Watch Ultra 4 could lean more than ever into health and fitness tracking.

New S-class chip, the first built in AI era

Last year’s Apple Watch models used the same S10 chip that first debuted in 2024. But the last time the Watch got a truly meaningful speed and performance bump was 2023.

Rumors indicate Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12 will have a brand new, more powerful chip—likely dubbed S11 or S12.

The timing lines up perfectly with Siri AI’s debut in watchOS 27. And no doubt, the first CPU boost in an S-class chip since 2023 will pack improvements that benefit AI features.

There’s a lot of potential for Apple Watch to be the first mass-market AI wearable. I’m excited to see how the new chip might help move that needle.

Wildcard: Design updates

	

There are conflicting reports concerning Apple Watch Ultra 4’s design. While Digitimes claims a redesign is coming, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said last month: “None of this year’s watches is expected to get a major design overhaul.”

We do know that a ceramic case option is expected for Apple Watch Series 12. So it’s possible that Apple will similarly offer something unique for Apple Watch Ultra 4’s design. Reporting is unclear, but perhaps we’ll see design updates that differentiate the latest Ultra model.

title: Anker’s Eufy Strides Into IFA With a New AI Ecosystem and Devices to Match
snippet: Anker’s security division has big plans, and the company is prepping an even bigger AI management system for your home — without relying on cloud data or subscriptions.
fullText:
Anker’s plans for home AI focus entirely on device algorithms.Anker

Anker and its home brand Eufy came to Berlin’s IFA event well prepared with major news, including an overhaul of how the company approaches home security, and the new capabilities it wants to give devices in the coming years. I’m no stranger to AI in home security, but Eufy’s approach is unique and has the potential to be particularly advantageous for customers.

Anker’s flagship announcement is an excellent example of what I’m talking about. We saw the company’s newest MindBase hub, a home AI enabler made to connect to many kinds of other Anker and Eufy products and process their data with AI algorithms, all entirely on-device. That means no connections to the cloud, few worries about how the company will use your private data for analysis and lower costs than most AI around the home.

Using Anker’s EasyOmni Link platform, the MindBase is supposed to connect to Anker’s security, energy, cleaning and audio devices. It also has Matter support, so devices that work with Apple Home, Amazon Alexa and Google Home are also on the table. The base uses an in-house-developed LLM running on an AI chip to accomplish much of what most companies need cloud help to do.

Eufy’s shiny new security tech sports the latest advances

Eufy’s new doorbell is pricey, but it has a 3K resolution and tracking.Anker Eufy

While Anker didn’t show off everything the MindBase is capable of, we did get some more advanced looks of its security capabilities thanks to Eufy’s new security line, set for the months to come. 

The MindBase itself, which is still pending price and release date info, can tap into Eufy’s new Smart Security Shield sensor with radar to detect strangers and encrypted facial data that can recognize familiar faces from up to 30 meters away. The on-device approach to facial data could help Eufy escape the privacy lawsuits similar to those facial data technologies are facing in the US.

Eufy is also releasing a new wired video doorbell, notable for its 3K resolution and AI tracking technology (meaning it can keep delivery people in view for longer, etc.). It’s set for sale at $300 later this month.

For those who want a full security setup, Eufy is also launching an eight-channel NVR system with 2K security cameras. I’m not sure how many NVR features will need MindBase to function, but Anker says the wired, fully contained kit can handle auto framing, smart video searches, cross-camera tracking and 24/7 recording.

Eufy’s line is also expanding into two particularly interesting security devices. One is a presence-sensing wall sensor made to detect falls, especially for those aging in place. The detector can raise alerts and link loved ones using two-way audio, a feature combination I’ve never seen before. The brand is also releasing a new $70 window camera later this year, a small 2.5K device with a cup-like shield design to reduce glare so people can attach it to the inside of a window.

I’ve tested cameras like these this year from brands like Wyze, and they’re an interesting compromise fit for apartment windows (such as those looking over your carport) and similar situations where an outdoor camera isn’t feasible. 

The big subscription question

I’ve seen the rise of window cams this year, now including Eufy’s.Anker Eufy

Anker’s Eufy brand has been one of my favorite options for no-subscription home security that still offers important features like human detection and local video storage without relying on the cloud. I’m not totally sure how the MindBase and new AI features will work, but there are promising signs.

For its new security cameras and sensors, Anker said, “The portfolio processes sensitive biometric data on-device … with no monthly subscriptions attached,” but added an important caveat that premium and optional features (not sure what those would be) may require a monthly fee, so there are a lot of questions for future details to answer.

For features like the MindBase’s MindSafe Memory, a local storage system that can perform AI searches through photos, videos and files, Anker didn’t mention any fee information, and I’m not sure if it will require a subscription. The same is true of the facial recognition features in the Smart Security Shield, although Eufy indicated earlier this summer that those features wouldn’t require a subscription, so I’m hopeful.

Anker also said it’s planning on adding new AI agents in addition to the security tricks, like an energy version to save power and a cleaning version to manage your robot vacuums, but I don’t have any info on whether those capabilities will require subscriptions.

A final important note about the Eufy brand

Anker showed up at IFA with plenty to test out in the coming year, as well as news about its branding plans. In the future, Anker has plans to congregate its brand names primarily under Anker. That means I may not be using the years-old Eufy name for too much longer.

Hints of this change were visible in Anker’s IFA showcases. For example, while the MindBase bears the Eufy name on the physical hub, Anker solely refers to it as the Anker MindBase in promotional materials, possibly a sign of things to come. I’ll keep you updated so the naming system doesn’t get too confusing when you’re looking for home security.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Tyler Lacoma
						

						

							Editor / Home Security and Smart Home						
					

											

								

											Tyler has worked on, lived with and tested all types of smart home and security technology for over a dozen years, explaining the latest features, privacy tricks, and top recommendations.
With degrees in Business Management, Literature and Technical Writing, Tyler takes every opportunity to play with the latest AI technology, push smart devices to their limits and occasionally throw cameras off his roof, all to find the best devices to trust in your life. He always checks with the renters (and pets) in his life to see what smart products can work for everyone, in every living situation. 
Living in beautiful Bend, Oregon gives Tyler plenty of opportunities to test the latest tech in every kind of weather and temperature. But when not at work, he can be found hiking the trails, trying out a new food recipe for his loved ones, keeping up on his favorite reading, or gaming with good friends.

title: Nvidia confirms it will buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion
snippet: Nvidia said Hugging Face hosts over 3 million models and is used by over 18 million developers.
fullText:
After weeks of swirling rumors, Nvidia confirmed today that it has acquired Hugging Face for $12.93 billion. Hugging Face’s platform hosts three million models, one million applications used by over 18 million developers, and half a million datasets.

In a blog post, Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang said that Hugging Face will continue to support open-source and open-weight models and will work on expanding developer access.

“Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem. Developers will choose the models they want, the frameworks they want, the clouds and inference service providers they want and the computing platforms they want. Nvidia compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face,” said Huang.

Huang touted Nvidia’s contributions and said that the chip company has released more than 500 models and 250 open datasets on Hugging Face. He argued that the company builds open models to get developers across the world to use them.

For a company like Nvidia, which is a dominant hardware platform for AI development and inference, an open ecosystem that it controls is beneficial as it can create a platform suited for its chips. Plus, as TechCrunch wrote earlier, Nvidia will be able to sell its unused capacity to enterprise customers packaged with Hugging Face’s offering.

Hugging Face was founded in 2016 and has raised over $395 million in funding to date, according to Crunchbase. The company’s last round was in 2023, when it raised $235 million led by Salesforce Ventures, with investments from Google, Amazon, IBM, and Nvidia.

In a post on X, Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue thanked the community for showing the company could be an alternative to closed-source APIs. 

“But for it to happen at [a] larger scale, it needs more compute, more support, more collaboration, and more visibility. That’s why we went to talk to Jensen, who offered to do exactly that with us,” said Delangue.

Hugging Face has risen in prominence, with more models being released every day. Last year, the company rejected a $500 million deal from Nvidia, according to the Financial Times. Last month, The Information reported that Hugging Face is clocking $150 million in annualized revenue. 

In an interview with TechCrunch in July, Delangue said that its growth rate is helping the platform to get “close to profitability.”

title: Poco F9 Pro and F9 Ultra launch with 185Hz panels, 8 Elite Gen 5 chips, and huge batteries
snippet: Xiaomi sub-brand Poco is officially expanding its flagship smartphone line with the launch of the Poco F9 Pro and Poco F9 Ultra. more…
fullText:
Xiaomi sub-brand Poco is officially expanding its flagship smartphone line with the launch of the Poco F9 Pro and Poco F9 Ultra.

Under the hood, the top-tier Poco F9 Ultra packs Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor paired with up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of UFS 4.1 storage. The standard Poco F9 Pro relies on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V Series (SM8850-1-AB) with up to 12GB of RAM and 512GB of storage. Both handsets incorporate a dedicated 12nm VisionBoost D8 graphics chip to handle AI frame insertion and super-resolution processing.

On the front, both devices feature HyperRGB AMOLED panels with a 185Hz refresh rate and peak brightness up to 4,500 nits. The Poco F9 Pro features a 6.59-inch display with a 2510 x 1156 resolution, while the Poco F9 Ultra expands to a 6.9-inch display with a 2608 x 1200 resolution. Both screens feature 480Hz 10-point touch sampling, 4800Hz instant touch sampling, Gorilla Glass 7i protection, and integrated ultrasonic fingerprint sensors.

Camera hardware sees a major overhaul on both models, starting with a shared 200MP primary sensor with optical image stabilization (OIS) and 4K video recording. The secondary camera configurations branch off from there. 

	

The Poco F9 Pro pairs the main camera with a 50MP floating telephoto lens capable of 2.5x optical zoom and an 8MP ultra-wide sensor. The Poco F9 Ultra steps up to a 50MP periscope telephoto lens with 5x optical zoom alongside a 50MP ultra-wide sensor. Both phones include a 32MP front-facing selfie camera.

Audio performance has been tuned in partnership with Bose. The F9 Pro comes equipped with symmetrical dual stereo speakers, whereas the Poco F9 Ultra introduces a 2.1-channel audio configuration that combines dual stereo speakers with an independent 1620 rear subwoofer.

Power endurance is handled by a 6,330mAh battery on the F9 Pro, while the F9 Ultra houses a, frankly, massive 8,050mAh silicon-carbon battery with a 16% silicon content ratio. Both models share the same charging speeds: 100W wired fast charging, 50W wireless charging, 27W wired reverse charging, and 22.5W wireless reverse charging.

Additional standard hardware specifications include IP68 dust and water resistance, NFC support, and Xiaomi HyperOS 3 running out of the box. Color choices for the F9 Pro include Black, White, and Aurora Green, which features a glow-in-the-dark rear cover. The F9 Ultra is available in Black and Dark Cherry with a glass fiber finish and interactive lighting accents on the rear housing.

Pricing for the Poco F9 Pro starts at $699 for the 12GB/256GB base model (early-bird $649) and reaches $769 for the 12GB/512GB tier (early-bird $699). The Poco F9 Ultra starts at $799 for the 12GB/256GB option (early bird $729), $949 for the 16GB/512GB option (early bird $799), and tops out at $1,199 for the 16GB/1TB option (early bird $1,059). Global availability and localized ordering options are available directly on the official Poco Global page and Xiaomi launch portal.

Devices and Consumer will include search and advertising revenues from LinkedIn and search advertising, as well as rev … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Microsoft is changing how it reports its finances to investors by splitting its businesses into two segments and disclosing quarterly revenue for its Azure cloud business for the first time. The changes are meant to reflect the ongoing impact of AI on Microsoft and how the company now operates.

The software giant has previously reported revenue from three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. This is now simplifying to two: Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.

Devices and Consumer will include search and advertising revenues from LinkedIn and search advertising, as well as revenue from the Xbox division and Windows OEM and devices. Agents and Infra is essentially the rest of Microsoft, including Azure, Microsoft 365 Cloud, Microsoft 365 commercial and consumer, server products, industry solutions, and the enterprise and partner services that Microsoft now calls frontier and support services.

“There’s no question AI represents a profound shift in both technology and business,” says Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. “It is changing what we build and how we operate, and it is blurring the boundaries between our products and reshaping our business models.”

The biggest change to this reporting structure will see Microsoft finally disclose how its Azure business is running on a quarterly basis. Microsoft has been providing year-over-year growth rates for its Azure business, reporting its Azure revenue for the first time last year. Azure revenue will no longer include GitHub cloud and other developer cloud services, nor Security Copilot and Healthcare and Life Sciences cloud revenues.

“Under this reporting structure, Azure becomes more purely our consumption-based platform and infrastructure business,” says Nadella. “Within each of these segments, you will have full transparency of quarterly revenue across each of our key businesses, including Azure, M365 Cloud, industry solutions, and ads.”

Microsoft will start using these new financial reporting changes during its first quarter fiscal 2027 earnings in late October.

title: Wonderful more than doubles its valuation to $5B in under 6 months
snippet: Wonderful said it will use its $550 million Series C funding to develop products faster, expand its FDE teams, and meet demand for its products.
fullText:
Israeli-Dutch AI startup Wonderful has raised $550 million in a Series C funding round that gives it a price tag of $5 billion, more than doubling the $2 billion valuation the company gained when it last raised funding nearly six months ago.

Insight Partners returned to lead this round, too, and existing investors Index Ventures, IVP, Vine Ventures, 9Yards, and Bessemer Venture Partners are participating once again. Salesforce is investing in the company for the first time in this round.

Founded in early 2025, Wonderful has grown blazingly fast. It initially saw strong traction with its customer service AI agent platform, which it built and customized to sell in various non-English-speaking markets. Its strategy of deploying engineering teams to work with its customers, sometimes on their premises, to deploy and integrate its AI tech into their workflows and systems also proved very successful. The company says it now works across more than 35 countries.

The startup’s core offering has evolved over the past few months, though. Departing from its customer service roots, Wonderful now offers a platform, dubbed “Wonderful AI OS,” which it says can coordinate and connect agents, workflows, and AI applications with companies’ data, context, and existing integrations. The company says the platform works with any AI model and is compatible with existing tech stacks.

“Customers can adopt whichever parts of the platform make the most sense, integrate them with existing systems, choose the best models for each workload, and retain ownership of everything they build,” Roey Lalazar, Wonderful CTO and co-founder, said in a statement.

The company is still leaning on its forward-deployed engineers to help embed its products quickly into companies — which appears to be a good strategy given the demand for experts versed in implementing AI services and products.

Wonderful said it will use the fresh $550 million to develop products faster, expand its FDE teams, and meet demand for its products.
