title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe’s Surprise Switch 2 Update Brings Multiplayer Mayhem
snippet: The surprise update adds eight-player, split-screen competition and other enhancements to Nintendo’s long-running kart racer.
fullText:
Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is seemingly the game that Nintendo refuses to move on from. The racing game, originally released on the Wii U back in 2014 and then updated for the Nintendo Switch in 2017, has received what might be the greatest update for the game that could get players back on the track.

Nintendo on Tuesday unexpectedly dropped the version 4.0.0 update for Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, which adds a new eight-player, split-screen option when playing the game on the Nintendo Switch 2, as well as CameraPlay support and support for higher-resolution TVs. It’s the new multiplayer option that has gone viral on social media, as gamers try to wrap their heads around playing an eight-player race on the Switch 2’s 7.9-inch screen.

While this split-screen mode can work on the Switch 2 in handheld mode, it’s clear that the new multiplayer option is designed for gamers to play with friends on a TV. It expands Mario Kart 8 Deluxe’s multiplayer beyond the four-player limit it has had since launch. Instead, up to eight racers can play together, with each racer able to have their own individual Joy-Con, Switch Pro Controller or Switch 2 Pro Controller. Those who paid the $25 for the Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass will also have access to all 96 courses in the VS Race multiplayer mode.

CameraPlay support was also added on Tuesday. This feature, which made its debut on the Switch 2, lets players connect a USB camera to their console during multiplayer and online matches so other players can see their faces while playing. Nintendo sells an official USB camera for the console, but there are many alternatives that work just as well. 

Another welcome change in the update is shortened loading times when playing on the Switch 2. Players should notice it takes less time to start races and battles when playing. 

This update for Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is part of Nintendo’s initiative to update its Switch games and optimize them for the Switch 2. On Monday, Pikmin 3 Deluxe received a similar update to match the resolution of the newer handheld console.

Tuesday’s update coincided with the Switch 2’s new price tag of $500. Nintendo announced the price jump of its newest console back in May, citing “changes in market conditions.”

Gaming hardware companies such as Nintendo, Sony, Microsoft and Valve have had to deal with the rising costs of components, mainly memory and storage, in what’s been dubbed RAMaggeddon. So far, there’s no sign that the memory shortage driving these price increases will end anytime soon.

title: Android still dominates global smartphone sales; Google’s Pixel 10a shines in one country
snippet: Updated data shows that, yep, Android is still the dominant force in the global smartphone market, but country-by-country breakdowns would hint otherwise – and Google’s Pixel series really only breaks into the conversation in one country, too. more…
fullText:
Updated data shows that, yep, Android is still the dominant force in the global smartphone market, but country-by-country breakdowns would hint otherwise – and Google’s Pixel series really only breaks into the conversation in one country, too.

Counterpoint Research published a breakdown of global smartphone OS share, measured by sales, with Android taking the win by a mile. On the global scale, Android makes up about 75% of smartphone sales compared to iOS, which makes up 20%. The last 5% is Huawei’s HarmonyOS. Q2 2026’s numbers aren’t that different from the same time last year, with Android down from 79%, ceding 4% to Apple and 1% to Huawei.

Counterpoint Research

The report brings out that the popularity of the Galaxy S26 series, the Ultra in particular, helped in “mitigating” Android’s overall decline amid RAMageddon’s impact on the market. 

Android’s sales share fell 4% YoY in Q2 2026 to 75%, as competition from iOS and HarmonyOS intensified. The Samsung Galaxy S26 series performed better than its predecessor, mitigating the overall decline in Android’s share. Chinese Android OEMs are shifting their focus to higher-value devices and scaling back activity in the entry-level segment to navigate RAM shortages and rising costs.

Meanwhile, another Counterpoint report breaks down the top five best-selling smartphones in major markets across the globe in Q2 2025, with most markets seeing Apple’s iPhone 17 series up on top. That includes, Japan, which stands out on the list because right behind the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17E is Google’s Pixel 10a, the only place Google stands out in all of this talk about top-selling phones. The Pixel 10a made up 7% of Japan’s smartphone sales in Q2, continuing a trend of popularity among Google’s budget-conscious Pixel in the region. It’s also noteworthy as the Pixel 9a didn’t make the same list this time last year.

title: The New York Times Just Dropped a Brand-New Wordle Spin-Off
snippet: Wordle in 1 is included in a group of bonus puzzles that will arrive every Wednesday.
fullText:
Wordle fans, start marking your calendars for hump day. 

On Wednesday, the New York Times introduced a weekly drop of five to six new puzzles created by the newspaper’s puzzle constructors and editors. The new puzzles aren’t daily but will be released every Wednesday in a group and will include twists on current puzzles. They’re only available to people who pay for a New York Times Games or All Access subscription.

The types of bonus puzzles offered may vary from week to week. Other puzzles, including Wordle, Connections, Strands, Pips, and Connections: Sports Edition, remain free, while some others are behind a paywall.

CNET offers daily hints and answers for Wordle, Connections, Strands, Connections: Sports Edition and the Mini Crossword.

Wordle in 1

I played the new batch of games, and I think the most popular game will be Wordle in 1. Regular Wordle gives you six tries to guess a five-letter word, uses specific colors to indicate if you’ve guessed a letter that’s included, and also notes if you put it in the right spot. Wordle in 1 sets up five five-letter grids, each with a different word, and fills them in with some correct and some incorrect letters. You use the letters provided to figure out the answers.

Wordle in 1 provides you with some correct and some incorrect letters, and you take it from there.NYT/Screenshot by CNET

In the example above, the colored letters indicate that the U and T are in the right spaces, that there’s no N at all, and the S and the other T needs to be relocated. (Answer at the bottom of this post if you want a spoiler.)

More games: Connections 3×3, Colorful Strands

Other games in the weekly drop also play off the current New York Times puzzles.

Connections 3×3 is a smaller version of the regular Connections puzzle, offering just nine words or phrases that you have to separate into three groups.

Colorful Strands is exactly the same as regular Strands, but the answers show up in color, which is something the regular puzzle does from time to time.

Mystery Mini is another Mini Crossword, with a creative twist. The first one, for example, uses two answers twice, with different clues, and other answers are also related.

Easy Mode Crossword simply takes the standard Friday crossword and just makes the clues easier. There’s also a monthly Special Crossword, which might be written in collaboration with a famous person or feature a theme. Comedian Rachel Dratch, a former Saturday Night Live cast member, co-constructed a puzzle released Tuesday.

That promised spoiler

Spoiler for the pictured Wordle in 1 puzzle above: The answer is TRUST.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Gael Cooper

She's been a journalist since 1989, working at Mpls.St.Paul Magazine, Twin Cities Sidewalk, the Minneapolis Star Tribune, and NBC News Digital. She's Gen X in birthdate, word and deed. fullText:

The Pixel Watch 5 goes from CD5A.260611.008 to CP3A.260905.002. This remains Wear OS 7 based on Android 17.

Gemini Personalization 

Personalization makes Gemini on Watch more helpful by learning from past conversations and connected Google apps (Gmail, Calendar, Search, YouTube, Photos) to deliver personalized responses. Users can ask queries like “What’s on my calendar today?” or “Find the tracking number in my email” and receive answers tailored to their data. The feature is powered by an offline user profile and real-time online retrieval working together. 

Proactive suggestions1

Gemini Intelligence Proactive Suggestions turns complex, multi-step tasks into seamless one-tap actions in messages. If a loved one asks when is the dinner with family, Gemini automatically locates the info in your calendar and surfaces it directly on your wrist, eliminating the need to dig through your phone

Offline Gemini 

Powered by on-device AI, Gemini can process core actions instantly with low latency, even when you’re completely offline. Examples are setting up a timer, starting/stopping a workout, turning on do not disturb and other device actions.

Raise to talk improvements

snippet: New Apple CEO John Ternus has just sent his first company-wide memo. fullText:
New Apple CEO John Ternus has just sent his first company-wide memo. In it, Ternus thanks Tim Cook and recognizes that Apple is “so lucky to have had a CEO who led with his values and with such decency and humanity.”

“We have a huge launch next week that’s going to be phenomenal,” Ternus also says, in reference to Apple’s forthcoming “Surprise and shine” special event.

Read the full memo, obtained by 9to5Mac, below. 

Ternus also looks further ahead in message, teasing the “incredible products already in the works and the ones we haven’t even imagined yet.”

Here is the full memo from Ternus sent to Apple employees today. 

Team,

Today, on my first day as CEO, I just wanted to send a quick note to thank everyone for the warm wishes. I also want to extend my deep appreciation to Tim for sharing so much of his knowledge and experience during this transition, and more importantly, for everything he contributed to Apple over the years. We’re so lucky to have had a CEO who led with his values and with such decency and humanity. We are all better for it, and I’m so grateful he’ll be our executive chairman.

I’m honored to be stepping into this role at what is truly the greatest company in the world, and I am so excited about everything we have in store. We have a huge launch next week that’s going to be phenomenal. Thanks for everything you’ve all done to make it possible.

I’m just as excited about what lies beyond that, including the incredible products already in the works and the ones we haven’t even imagined yet that we’ll dream up and create together. There’s no team in the world I’d rather build the future with.

More to come. In the meantime, thanks for your excellent work!

John

title: Dell’s new 14S laptop exists to challenge MacBook Neo and, somehow, might be even cheaper
snippet: Apple’s MacBook Neo has made waves in the laptop world because it’s a remarkably well-built and reliable laptop at a very affordable price – though one that’s a bit higher now thanks to RAMageddon. Dell is ready to challenge that with its new Dell 14S laptop announced at IFA, and it somehow might be even cheaper. more…
fullText:
Apple’s MacBook Neo has made waves in the laptop world because it’s a remarkably well-built and reliable laptop at a very affordable price – though one that’s a bit higher now thanks to RAMageddon. Dell is ready to challenge that with its new Dell 14S laptop announced at IFA, and it somehow might be even cheaper.

The Dell 14S is directly positioned as an “affordable” laptop for “students, college, and everyday life.” It features an aluminum build, 21 hours of battery life, and either an Intel Core Ultra 3 or Core Ultra 5 processor. The 16:10 display has 60Hz and 120Hz options while the hardware has two USB-C ports and an HDMI port, as well as a headphone jack. 

Dell says the 14S weighs in at around 2.5lbs and is just 13.5mm thick. 

In a Q&A on its blog, Dell directly positions the 14S as a “compelling” alternative to the MacBook Neo, though pricing hasn’t actually been announced at this point. The company hints, though, that it will be cheaper than the XPS 13 that already starts at $699 – in other words, Dell 14S might just be cheaper than the MacBook Neo.

	

The Dell 14S is available in the United States this fall. Pricing will be announced closer to availability in each market. What we can say is that the Dell 14S is designed to be complementary to XPS 13 and accessible for students and young adults globally. We’re committed to making sure regional pricing reflects that too.

Amusingly, Dell acknowledges that it already launched a laptop called the “14S” earlier this year, saying that the “old” one is designed for creators, while this “new” model “prioritizes everyday performance, long battery life, portability, colorful design and accessible pricing.” Perfectly not confusing.

title: Samsung’s latest Galaxy Book 6 starts at $799 with 8GB of RAM
snippet: Samsung is launching a new laptop in its Galaxy Book 6 series, and it’s much more affordable with a starting price of $799. more…
fullText:
Samsung is launching a new laptop in its Galaxy Book 6 series, and it’s much more affordable with a starting price of $799.

Announced this week, the latest Galaxy Book 6 release is a mid-tier version of Samsung’s laptop, cutting down on some key specs in order to hit a lower price point. Where the current lowest-priced option is a 14-inch (IPS) Galaxy Book 6 with 512GB of storage, 16GB of RAM, and an Intel Core Ultra 5 chip, the new model takes everything a step down with:

14-inch LCD display

Intel Core 3 or Core 5 processor

8GB or 16GB of RAM

256GB/512GB/1TB of storage

It’s a notable step down, but at considerable savings. Where that previously mentioned Book 6 starts at $1,249 in the US, this new release will start at $799 – $100 more than the MacBook Neo. 

The hardware measures in at 15.7mm thick, just shy of 3lbs, and has a 61.2Wh battery inside – Samsung claims 25 hours of battery life – with 45W USB-C charging. There are two USB-C ports, a USB-A port, an HDMI port, and a headphone/microphone jack. Samsung is also introducing a new “Violet Silver” color in addition to the usual grey.  It runs Windows 11 with Samsung’s usual suite of added apps that include a lot of integrations with Galaxy smartphones. 

	

Samsung’s new Galaxy Book 6 is available already in some markets, but not the US just yet. It’ll be available on Samsung.com and Amazon in the States starting October 5.

fullText:
Today is September 1st, and Apple has officially handed over the reins of CEO from Tim Cook to John Ternus. This commences a new era with Ternus leading the company. 

You can see the change reflected on the company’s newly-updated leadership page, with Ternus getting the CEO title and Cook moving to the Board of Directors section in his new role as Executive Chair.

Ternus’ rise to the top job is expected to herald a shift in company strategy, with a more product-oriented vision compared to Cook’s operational expertise. However, these changes take time to trickle down. His first public-facing role will be to introduce the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra lineup at the company’s fall media event, scheduled for September 9. 

Previously, the board of directors were listed on the leadership website by name only. Alongside Cook joining their ranks, Apple has expanded the section to include profile headshots as well. 

The board of directors consists of Tim Cook, Arthur Levinson, Wanda Austin, Alex Gorsky, Andrea Jung, Monica Lozano, Ron Sugar, Sue Wagner, and John Ternus (who gets a board seat as CEO).

title: Apple Watch Series 12: Three new features coming next week
snippet: Apple Watch Series 12 is coming next week, launching at the September event alongside Apple Watch Ultra 4. Here are three new features rumored for Apple Watch Series 12. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch Series 12 is coming next week, launching at the September event alongside Apple Watch Ultra 4. Here are three new features rumored for Apple Watch Series 12.

#1: New S-class chip

Apple’s S-class chips don’t get meaningful updates very often. Even though Apple does change the number most years, actual CPU improvements are rare. And last year, the company skipped offering an S11 altogether and kept the S10 around.

But this year, rumors indicate an upgraded S-class chip is coming to Apple Watch Series 12. Likely named S12 or S11, it will be more powerful, faster, and also the first new Watch chip of the AI era.

Siri AI is a tentpole addition to watchOS 27, and it’s expected to run best on the new chip. But other everyday features should benefit from the new chip too.

#2: Always-on heart rate sensor and more health improvements

Apple Watch Series 12 has long been rumored to add new health features. For example, the FDA reportedly reviewed an upgrade to hypertension notifications that’s expected to debut next week.

One other specific rumor is that the heart rate sensor will get always-on support. This would match functionality offered by competing products like WHOOP.

Per Mark Gurman, the new Series 12 sensor can “continuously collect data throughout the day — not just when it senses you’re doing intense activity or at other random intervals.”

#3: Ceramic case option, likely in white and dark gray

Joining the usual new watch bands and case options, Apple is expected to debut a Ceramic case for the first time since 2019’s Series 5 model. 

Apple will reportedly offer Series 12 in two Ceramic colors: white and dark gray. Per Bloomberg: “Apple has tested both white and dark gray configurations for the Series 12 ceramic cases.”

It’s unclear how much of a premium Ceramic will add to the Series 12 price, but the last time it was offered, it started at $1,299—far more than Apple Watch Ultra costs today.

title: Galaxy S26 FE is $699 with last year’s specs, Android 17, and a few new features
snippet: Debuting with a higher price tag and effectively the same spec sheet, the Galaxy S26 FE might as well be a poster child for living through “RAMageddon.” more…
fullText:
Debuting with a higher price tag and effectively the same spec sheet, the Galaxy S26 FE might as well be a poster child for living through “RAMageddon.”

Samsung has just unveiled its new Galaxy S26 FE, with the “Fan Edition” device offering more or less an identical set of specs compared to last year’s Galaxy S25 FE – 6.7-inch FHD+ AMOLED display, Exynos 2500 chip, 8GB of RAM (128GB/256GB storage), a 4,900 mAh battery with 45W charging, and a triple camera setup on the back comprised of a 50MP main, 12MP ultrawide, and 8MP telephoto (3x). 

Outside of a chipset generation bump, the only new thing this year, at least on paper, is that the Galaxy S26 FE runs Android 17 (One UI 9) out of the box, an update only available otherwise on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series (and Flip 8). The software packs some added features, too, such as the “My FanCam” that tracks a subject in video for social sharing, new AI features powered by Gemini Omni, and more.

Samsung has also updated the design this year, with a new camera bump look that’s closer to the rest of the Galaxy S26 series. It also comes in “Blueberry,” “Graphite,” and “Pistachio” colorways.

	

It’s a tough sell, to say the least, given Galaxy S25 FE launched for $50 less last year, and currently sells for as little as $500 outright through some carriers and retailers. But that’s just life during “RAMageddon,” ain’t it?

Galaxy S26 FE will be available on September 4.

title: Pixel 11 series getting early September update, not Android 17 QPR1
snippet: We’re expecting the stable release of Android 17 QPR1 in September. Before that, Google is rolling out an out-of-cycle update to the Pixel 11 series with a September 2026 security patch. more…
fullText:
We’re expecting the stable release of Android 17 QPR1 in September. Before that, Google is rolling out an out-of-cycle update to the Pixel 11 series with a September 2026 security patch.

On Tuesday afternoon, Pixel 11 series users received an OTA update to CD1A.260905.001.A1 (from CD1A.260714.001.A9). 

The Android security update level is “September 1, 2026.” (Note: Not September 5.) The install screen has the usual generic security message: “This update fixes critical bugs and improves the performance and stability of your device.”

So far, we have reports of an under 100 MB OTA hitting the Pixel 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold. Google has yet to post factory or OTA images as of Tuesday afternoon.

	

This is not Android 17 QPR1. Several of the visual changes coming in that release are not yet present, so this is still the initial release of Android 17.

Rather, Google is likely rolling out this update as a hot patch for Pixel 11 issues discovered since last month’s launch. The fact Google did not wait for Android 17 QPR1 should be telling.

title: Google Maps has renamed ‘Lake America’ for users in the US
snippet: Following an executive order late last week, Google Maps has updated its label for “Lake Ontario” to “Lake America.” more…
fullText:
Following an executive order late last week, Google Maps has updated its label for “Lake Ontario” to “Lake America.”

If you are located within the United States, viewing “Lake Ontario” via Google Maps will now show the name “Lake America,” following last week’s executive order. 

Google, in a brief blog post, confirms that users in Canada will continue to see only “Lake Ontario” while users in other parts of the world will see “Lake Ontario (Lake America).” This can also be seen using a VPN.

From the United States
From Canada

Google continues to cite a policy in which it updates location names based on local government data; in this case, the US GNIS, where the name has been updated as of August 27 by the Department of the Interior following Trump’s order. Google referred to this same policy in February 2025 when it updated Maps to show “Gulf of America.”

	
	

Canada has confirmed that it will not be updating the name from “Lake Ontario,” with Prime Minister Mark Carney stating that “the name is more than 400 years ​old, predating ​both the Confederation of Canada ‌and ⁠the Declaration of Independence of the United States of ​America.” Carney added that the name comes “from the Wendat word Ontari’io, which, appropriately, means ‘the lake is beautiful, the lake is big.'”

Notably, competitor MapQuest has directly said it will not change the name, instead building out a name generator that allows users to create their own new names for the lake, mocking the change. Apple Maps is not yet showing the name either. Apple changed “Gulf of America” within a day or two of Google back in February, though.

Steep backlash pushed Google to limit new reviews of “Gulf of America” in 2025, but the same limitation has yet to be placed on “Lake America,” we observed in testing.

title: AirPods 5: Here’s what rumors say will launch next week
snippet: Rumors indicate AirPods 5 are launching next week alongside iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and iPhone Ultra. Here’s what we know so far about the new AirPods. more…
fullText:
Rumors indicate AirPods 5 are launching next week alongside iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and iPhone Ultra. Here’s what we know so far about the new AirPods.

AirPods 5 expected to launch at September 9 event in two models, but no cameras

Apple’s biggest event of the year is happening next week on September 9. Alongside new iPhones, Apple Watch models, and likely Home products, AirPods 5 are also expected to debut. 

AirPods 4 launched in 2024, and historically Apple has had two- or three-year gaps between generations. AirPods launched in 2016, AirPods 2 in 2019, AirPods 3 in 2021, and AirPods 4 in 2024. So from a timing standpoint, a launch this year more or less fits the pattern.

What’s surprising about the new AirPods, however, is how few rumors and leaks there have been about them.

Most AirPods rumors of late have centered on new models with cameras. A recent video leaked in Apple software showed the camera-equipped model in action, sparking speculation it would launch soon.

However, Mark Gurman at Bloomberg says AirPods with cameras will not arrive until 2027. But he’s expecting AirPods 5—without cameras—to debut at Apple’s September event. He recently wrote:

[Apple is] planning to debut fresh AirPods as early as the September product launch event. The rollout will include new AirPods 5, an update to Apple’s entry-level earbuds, the people said. That model was last refreshed in 2024. A camera-equipped version of the AirPods, meanwhile, isn’t expected until next year.

In a post on X, Gurman added that AirPods 5 will come in two distinct models:

with Active Noise Cancellation

without ANC

Previously in his reporting, Gurman wrote that he doesn’t anticipate AirPods 5 getting the heart-rate sensor from AirPods Pro 3, but Apple “is looking to add several more health features to the AirPods over time, including a temperature reader.” He also noted separately that Apple is “working on an H3 chip designed for less lag time and better audio quality.”

It’s unclear whether AirPods 5 will get the H3 chip or not. When Apple launched H2, it was exclusive to the AirPods Pro line initially.

But new health sensors are possible for AirPods 5, and H3 is a possibility too. Otherwise, details on AirPods 5 are minimal at this point. Perhaps like it did with AirPods Max 2 earlier this year, Apple will be able to surprise us with its AirPods 5 reveal.

fullText:
Following Magic Pointer and Desktop Camera, Google has now released a “Look up” app for Googlebooks.

Look up is roughly analogous to a similarly named macOS feature (“Look Up”) when you right-click.

snippet: Google has some interesting tests going on behind the scenes of Android Auto right now, but only one of them is likely to actually be released – a new quick settings menu. more…
fullText:
Google has some interesting tests going on behind the scenes of Android Auto right now, but only one of them is likely to actually be released – a new quick settings menu.

About APK Insight: In this “APK Insight” post, we’ve decompiled the latest version of an application that Google uploaded to the Play Store. When we decompile these files (called APKs, in the case of Android apps), we’re able to see various lines of code within that hint at possible future features. Keep in mind that Google may or may not ever ship these features, and our interpretation of what they are may be imperfect. We’ll try to enable those that are closer to being finished, however, to show you how they’ll look in case that they do ship. With that in mind, read on.

In a teardown of Android Auto 17.6, we can see Google setting the stage for an implementation of Quick Settings tiles in the car UI. Strings currently point to a “Do Not Disturb” tile, but it lays the groundwork for future additions.

<string name=”quick_settings_tile_dnd”>Do Not Disturb</string>

<string name=”quick_settings_toast_dnd_off”>Do Not Disturb turned off</string>

<string name=”quick_settings_toast_dnd_on”>Do Not Disturb turned on</string>

This is not currently user-facing within Android Auto, but the folks over at Android Authority manually activated the feature, showing that it appears in the notification tray.

	

While this feels like a natural addition for Android Auto and like something Google would actually release to users, the other addition in Android Auto 17.6 feels like a fun little joke at best.

“Jimothy,” the viral raccoon, is hiding in Android Auto with a flag for a “Jimothy mode.”

SystemUi__jimothy_mode_enabled

Enabling this one shows “Jimothy” with weather animations, showing the current temperature and conditions on top of your music widget. It’s hilarious and very fun, but also incredibly unlikely to be something Google actually releases to the public – if nothing else, the meme’s time has passed. 

But, Google, this should absolutely happen with “Froggy,” as it’d be a fun and fitting way to finally show weather data consistently on Android Auto.

title: US government sides with OpenAI on issue of training LLMs on copyrighted material
snippet: "The United States has a strong interest in continuing to develop a robust and competitive artificial intelligence industry that sets the standard for the practice and procedure of AI use globally," the brief reads.
fullText:
In a lawsuit that The New York Times filed against OpenAI, the Trump administration has contributed a 20-page brief in defense of the ChatGPT maker’s unlicensed use of copyrighted material to train its LLMs.

“The United States has a strong interest in continuing to develop a robust and competitive artificial intelligence industry that sets the standard for the practice and procedure of AI use globally… As such, it is critical for the United States to ‘retain global leadership in artificial intelligence,’” the brief reads, referencing an executive order that President Donald Trump signed last year.

The LLMs powering chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are trained on incomprehensibly massive databases of published works, including copyrighted books, articles, and other media that AI companies feed into these databases without permission. Many publishers, including The New York Times in this case, have sought to argue that it is illegal for AI companies like OpenAI to train AI models on their copyrighted material.

This question — can you use copyrighted material to train an AI? — isn’t black and white, hence the extensive legal debate around the subject. These conversations often center on fair use, a carve out of copyright law that makes exceptions for certain scenarios when it can be ruled legal to use someone else’s copyrighted work without permission. In this case, the fair use debate addresses whether AI companies’ use of copyrighted work is “transformative” enough for a judge to rule it legal.

“Constraining LLM development under a misunderstanding of fair use doctrine would thwart such creative and scientific progress while hindering American prosperity and economic mobility,” the brief says.

So far, cases about AI training and copyright infringement have largely been favorable to AI companies. Last year, Judge William Alsup ordered Anthropic to pay a $1.5 billion copyright settlement to a group of writers whose works were used to train the company’s AI models; but Anthropic wasn’t dinged for its AI training. Rather, the company was fined for using illegal shadow libraries to pirate the books it used for training.

“Like any reader aspiring to be a writer, Anthropic’s LLMs trained upon works not to race ahead and replicate or supplant them — but to turn a hard corner and create something different,” Judge Alsup wrote, comparing the LLM’s training to a human reading a book.

This new Trump administration brief is not a ruling, as the case is being tried in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, and the authors of the brief do not have jurisdiction. However, this intervention by the Trump administration could still carry weight.

title: Apple reveals ‘shocking evidence’ from ex-employee’s MacBook in OpenAI suit
snippet: Apple has filed a new document in its ongoing lawsuit against OpenAI as it continues to push for expedited discovery. In today’s filing, Apple says that it has new “shocking evidence” based on early forensic inspection of a laptop used by former engineer Chang Liu. more…
fullText:
Apple has filed a new document in its ongoing lawsuit against OpenAI as it continues to push for expedited discovery. In today’s filing, Apple says that it has new “shocking evidence” based on early forensic inspection of a laptop used by former engineer Chang Liu.

Apple first filed the lawsuit in July, accusing ex-employees of stealing trade secrets for the benefit of OpenAI. It moved for a preliminary injunction a few weeks later, while also asking the court to expedite discovery, including early document production and depositions of key OpenAI employees and executives. Apple again emphasized the need for expedited discovery last week. OpenAI has called for dismissal. 

As covered before, Chang Liu is one of the parties named in Apple’s lawsuit. Liu was a senior system electrical engineer at Apple who left the company for OpenAI in January. The lawsuit alleges that Liu exploited a security bug to download confidential engineering files after leaving.

In today’s filing, Apple says that Liu’s lawyers recently handed over his MacBook that he used after leaving Apple. According to Apple, an “initial forensic analysis” of that MacBook revealed four things, quoted from Apple’s filing:

Mr. Liu not only downloaded a confidential Apple circuit schematic but also used it in his work at OpenAI;

Far from his unauthorized access to Apple’s third-party cloud storage being unknown to him, Mr. Liu and others at OpenAI were well-aware of that access;

Mr. Liu, upon learning of Apple’s internal investigation of him, sent instructions for destroying evidence to an OpenAI colleague who confirmed she would comply; and

Mr. Liu used a tool in his work at OpenAI that has the same name as an internal Apple engineering application used for Apple development work.

Apple alleges that Liu ran a simulation in March using the circuit schematic file in LTspice, an electrical engineering tool. In messages from around that time, Liu said his AI “agent” learned to run LTspice and review the results.

Apple argues that when trade secret information is fed into an AI agent or model that learns from it, that learning “may create irreversible and continually propagating uses of the trade secret.”

Apple says the defendants decided not to inspect the laptop and instead chose to “advance theories that the device’s data disproves.” 

Additionally, Apple learned about Liu’s use of the schematic because he used it on a Mac mini which later synced via iCloud to the MacBook he took from Apple. Apple now also wants access to that Mac mini. 

This “shocking evidence” is yet another point in favor of expedited discovery in the case, Apple says:

“This shocking evidence—which Defendants chose to ignore despite its availability—demonstrates why Apple urgently needs expedited discovery. The MacBook represents the very limited information Defendants provided so far (and only after weeks of delay), and shows Apple is not conducting ‘fishing expeditions’ but that its trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed.”

title: Narwal’s New Robot Vacuums and Floor Cleaners Are All About Better Mopping
snippet: Mops that can remove old and dried stains are everyone’s concern at IFA Berlin this year.
fullText:
Narwal has made some of the best robot vacuums and wet and dry mops we’ve tested here at CNET. Most recently, we were impressed by the Narwal Flow 2 and its impressive object avoidance and recognition, which earned it a spot on our best list. Narwhal’s new lineup, revealed at IFA Berlin 2026, features more models that continue to build on perfecting what works rather than revolutionary changes. 

The big news here is that Narwal’s FlowWash mopping, which used to be only on the flagship Flow series, is trickling its way down to other units in the lineup, like the Freo 20 and Freo 20 Edge. This is something we’ve seen happen across the industry. 

“For a decade, we’ve focused on making mopping truly effective in robotic cleaning. The Flow 2 represents the pinnacle of that journey, and with this new lineup, we’re bringing the expertise behind it to more homes while expanding into new cleaning categories,” Junbin Zhang, Founder and CEO of Narwal, said in a press statement.

Like other companies, Narwal considers mopping one of the biggest challenges for the robot vacuum industry, especially with the new focus on removing old, dried stains. Its FlowWash mopping system is one we’ve seen on other models, in which the mop roller is continuously refreshed and cleaned. 

Specifically with the FlowWash, the models include a microfiber flatted roller mop that the company says provides more consistent floor contact for stain removal. It also uses 16 angled water nozzles to refresh the mop with hot water during cleaning and an integrated scraper to remove dirt and wastewater. Finally, it has 12 newtons of downward pressure, which isn’t as high as some other robot vacuums we’ve seen at IFA, but it should get the job done, especially for models that shouldn’t cost as much. 

With the Freo 20, you get the mopping features, plus 31,000 pascals of suction power. There’s also improved navigation with dual RGB cameras and AI recognition of more than 300 household objects. Narwal says this model is designed for larger living spaces and more complex home environments.

With the Freo 20 Edge, you don’t get the more advanced AI object and clutter recognition, making it more suitable for apartments and less complicated spaces. However, it also has FlowWash, 31,000 pascals of suction, lidar, and structured light 3D navigation, a slim 9.5-centimeter body to get under furniture and a self-emptying and cleaning docking station. These are all higher-end features we used to see on flagships that are

Cordless and wet dry vacuums 

The Narwal V50 Cube is the company’s new cordless vacuum that comes with an auto-empty docking station, a feature that I loved on the Levoit Aero. The dock is compact and lightweight, while the V50 Cube still has 210 air watts of suction to handle pet hair and dirt. 

On the wet and dry cleaning side, Narwal has an Essential Model for daily cleaning and a Flagship Model with all the bells and whistles. The flagship model comes with 400-degree-Celsius steam and 95-degree-Celsius hot-water mopping, once again focused on stain removal and sterilization. It has 25,000 pascals of suction power, a floating scraper and a sensor that can detect dirt and adjust suction based on the floor conditions. It can lie flat and run for 40 minutes in AI mode. 

Price and availability 

The new models will start launching in European markets in September. The upcoming wet-and-dry vacuum range will also see new models in 2027, with launch details to follow.

In the US, the Narwal Freo 20 has been available on narwal.com and Amazon since Aug. 20 for $1,099, with a launch price of $900 until Thursday. The Narwal Freo 20 Edge is available starting Sept. 7 at narwal.com and on Amazon for $800, with a launch price of $700 from Sept. 7 to Sept. 20.

The US pricing and availability for the Narwal V50 Cube and the Narwal wet-and-dry vacuum will be determined later.

fullText:
Anker has made some of our favorite and most innovative robot vacuums over the years, and recently, they’ve also been getting into robot lawn mowers, earning spots on our tested lists. The newest models they’re showing off at IFA Berlin 2026 include a robot vacuum and a robot mower, both with key improvements and features over previous generations. 

Anker’s newest robot vacuum — and potentially the last one to keep the Eufy name (more on that below) — is the Omni E35, and it just might be what my three asthmatic cats need because it focuses on sterilization and disinfection. Anker describes it as “baby-grade,” meaning it’s TÜV Rheinland-certified for the “Maternal and Infant Cleaning Robot mark.” It can eliminate bacteria and dust mites, and it has low noise and high efficiency when it comes to cleaning and self-cleaning.   

Anker says it’s the first and only robot vacuum to earn the Asthma & Allergy Friendly Certification from the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America. This is especially interesting to me as someone who has the bad luck of having three cats diagnosed with asthma. The vet told me it was incredibly unlikely to occur naturally, so the cause is probably environmental — dust mites, dander, outdoor pollution, fragrances or smoke from the neighbors downstairs. At least a couple of those factors could be addressed by a robot vacuum capable of more thorough fine-dust pickup and sterilization, so I’m interested in seeing it in action and trying it at home.

Anker says the E35 Omni can clean your floors well enough for babies to play on.Anker

It has all the typical flagship features you’d expect from a top-tier model, including 35,000 pascals of suction and the Hydro Jet 2.0 self-cleaning roller mop. It also has a kitchen deep clean mode that uses an algorithm to determine how to tackle tougher stains, by saturating, soaking and then scrubbing. 

The Omni E35 will be available starting Sept. 25, though pre-orders will start Sept. 4. It’ll cost $1,100 at MSRP, but if you buy it during the early bird pricing, you can get it for $900. 

Eufy S2 Max

Anker

Also new in the robotics space is the Eufy S2 Max, Anker’s first robot mower developed entirely in-house. It has vision-based SLAM navigation and real-time 3D mapping, meaning no boundary wires or RTK beacons are required, which has become increasingly common in the robot mower market. It also has improved computing and full all-wheel drive, letting it handle terrain up to 80% slopes, a dual blade system and edge-to-edge cutting with an extendable trimming arm.  

US availability and pricing are still to be determined, but it’ll be available in EU markets in May 2027 for 3,999 euros. 

Anker is rebranding

Anker’s Eufy brand includes its lineup of robot vacuums and robot lawn mowers, as well as home security products. At IFA Berlin 2026, the company revealed that after 14 years of operation, it’s bringing all of its sub-brands, including Eufy and Soundcore for the audio products, under the Anker umbrella. In the future, all Anker products, no matter if they’re robot vacuums, robot lawn mowers, security cameras, smart doorbells or headphones, will be sold under the Anker brand. 

The change isn’t immediate, and an Anker representative who briefed me prior to IFA said that for a time, consumers in different markets will still see the distinct branding across product categories, but the goal is to consolidate it under Anker. For now, the lineup announced at IFA 2026 will continue to use the Eufy or Soundcore branding. The announcement coincides with the opening of an official Anker Flagship store in Berlin on Sept. 5, the company’s first standalone retail store there. 

I cover vacuums and home tech for CNET. While I’m here at IFA Berlin 2026, I’m determined to seek out the most interesting tech that solves your most common cleaning problems. I’m excited to see the Eufy Omni E35 and Eufy S2 Max. I’ll report back with my impressions later.

Editors’ note: Ajay Kumar’s travel costs for the IFA conference were covered by Roborock. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

title: Chrome’s Android navigation bar redesign has too much chrome
snippet: I quite like how Chrome for Android’s main interface has essentially remained the same since 2012. The consistency is refreshing as everything else on my phone changes. While I’m open to modernization, the latest attempt at a redesign suffers from too much chrome. more…
fullText:
I quite like how Chrome for Android’s main interface has essentially remained the same since 2012. The consistency is refreshing as everything else on my phone changes. While I’m open to modernization, the latest attempt at a redesign suffers from too much chrome.

When the browser launched in 2008, the name was meant to signify speed and a minimal graphical user interface, or chrome. On Android, that philosophy has persisted with just an address bar at the top or bottom of the screen. That text field can be flanked by various buttons, but the most minimal state consists of just the tab switcher and three-dot overflow menu. Over the years, Google has just refreshed these elements while keeping the placement unchanged.

Old vs. new

The upcoming redesign once again adds a secondary toolbar at the bottom of the screen that has buttons for your homepage (which can be disabled), Gemini, new tab, and the tab switcher. This lets Google add a dedicated back button to the left of the Omnibox, while the toolbar shortcut is now placed inside.

	

Google was close to launching a similar revamp in 2020, but ultimately abandoned it because “mainstream users” found it “disorienting.”

I don’t mind the Gemini shortcut, and think giving people a dedicated new tab button is a good idea. That was my toolbar shortcut of choice for ages, and Google is now showing a share button by default next to the URL. (Tip: Long-press on the address bar to quickly copy links.)

If you keep the address bar at the top, this interface is perfectly fine. However, as a bottom bar user, the stacked interface elements are just so thick. When you first scroll down a page and the interface auto-hides, it really hammers home how much web content Chrome is covering.

Things become downright ridiculous when viewing Tab Groups. Having three rows stacked on top of one another looks comical and makes your screen feel infinitely smaller. To me, this interface is not usable, and I’ve forced myself back to the top address bar. 

Simply making the bottom toolbar thinner would help a great deal. It would salvage this redesign and let Google stick to the browser’s namesake design.

This navigation bar redesign is slowly rolling out to the stable channel. It’s not clear whether Google has committed to this interface, but I hope it changes before launch. Ideally, Google would preserve the original interface as an option, but that seems unlikely.

title: iPhone Ultra release timing: Here’s what the latest reporting says
snippet: Apple will unveil its foldable iPhone Ultra next week at the September event, but it’s unclear exactly when the new model will ship to users. Here’s what to expect per the latest reporting. more…
fullText:
Apple will unveil its foldable iPhone Ultra next week at the September event, but it’s unclear exactly when the new model will ship to users. Here’s what to expect per the latest reporting.

iPhone Ultra is likely to ship in September, but with very limited availability per reporting

Next week, Apple will debut its first ever foldable iPhone model: the iPhone Ultra. 

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are coming too, expected to go on sale later that week ahead of wide availability September 18.

But even though iPhone Ultra will be announced at the same event, it’s still unclear if Apple’s foldable model will actually ship to users at the same time as iPhone 18 Pro.

There have been countless reports over the last several months regarding the launch timing for iPhone Ultra. Fortunately, the most recent reporting is optimistic that we’ll see the device ship in September—albeit with limited supply.

Earlier this month, Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital said supply will be “extremely limited” at launch, but per his sources in the supply chain, there’s no evidence of a delay past September.

Similarly, a July report in Cailian News Agency referenced conversations with Apple supply chain sources. “They said that there was no change in the delivery time date in September, denying rumors of product postponement.” ChannelNews Australia was another recent source saying the device would be available in September, at least in the US.

Looking further back though, the story changes. 

Ming Chi-Kuo predicted earlier in the summer that iPhone Ultra will follow a similar strategy to the iPhone X in 2017. Meaning it could be announced in September but ship later in the fall. Macworld heard a similar plan from its sources.

And back in April, Nikkei Asia stirred a lot of buzz by reporting the foldable could be delayed several months into 2027. Mark Gurman at Bloomberg refuted that report though, saying the device was still “on track” for September.

iPhone Ultra release timing: wrap-up

In summary, the more recent reporting indicates that iPhone Ultra will indeed ship in September. It might be available in very limited territories and quantities, but early adopters should be able to buy it soon.

When do you expect iPhone Ultra to launch? Let us know in the comments.

title: Leaker claims iPhone 18 Pro chip will have 7 GPU cores and faster RAM
snippet: A Chinese leaker with some track record has posted images of claimed circuit diagrams of the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro models. These suggest that the new A20 Pro chip may have seven GPU cores – one more than its predecessor – and a faster memory interface … more…
fullText:
A Chinese leaker with some track record has posted images of claimed circuit diagrams of the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro models.

These suggest that the new A20 Pro chip may have seven GPU cores – one more than its predecessor – and a faster memory interface … 

The images posted by Weibo user Fried White Rice are not of the A20 Pro chip itself, but rather diagrams of where the chip will be attached to the underlying circuit board. From this, they’re making inferences about the power and architecture of the new chip, drawing two main conclusions about likely improvements.

First, the diagrams point to six CPU cores in the same configuration as last year’s model: two high-performance ones and four efficiency cores. However, it appears that the cache memory for the efficiency cores has been increased.

We can see that the L2 cache for the small CPU cores has been increased—likely from 6 MB in the A19 Pro to 8 MB—while the L2 cache for the big CPU cores remains unchanged at 16 MB.

Trying to determine the number of GPU cores from the limited information provided by the solder diagrams is tricky, with six, seven and eight cores all possibilities. However, they conclude that seven cores is the most likely.

Again relying on the overall outline and solder‑ball positions, we can roughly deduce the GPU’s layout and explore several dozen configurations across three core counts—6, 7, and 8 cores. Ultimately, the 7‑core GPU configuration emerges as the most plausible arrangement.

Fixed Focus Digital recently suggested that the A20 Pro chip will be 18% faster than its predecessor with 30% better power efficiency.

9to5Mac’s Take

The Weibo account does have a certain amount of credibility, but this kind of indirect inference is very much a dark art. While the conclusions drawn are indeed plausible, they shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than informed guesses.

title: Google’s hyper-personalized ‘Dreambeans’ feed is now free to test
snippet: Dreambeans is an experimental app from Google Labs that will “proactively dream up personalized daily stories.” After previously requiring a subscription, Dreambeans is now available for free Google Accounts in the US to test. more…
fullText:
Dreambeans is an experimental app from Google Labs that will “proactively dream up personalized daily stories.” After previously requiring a subscription, Dreambeans is now available for free Google Accounts in the US to test.

Dreambeans is very much like a hyper-personalized Google Now or Discover feed. Like the Gemini app and AI Mode, it uses Google’s Personal Intelligence system to learn your interests by looking at your Gmail, Google Photos, Calendar, Workspace, Search history, and YouTube. During setup, you can choose which apps Dreambeans can access.

Workspace supplies ground-truth transaction data like receipts and upcoming flights

Photos provides the visual memories and insights about you and the people in your life

YouTube identifies your active hobbies

Search detects your budding interests

By combining all these unique signals, Dreambeans can proactively generate rich and highly customized daily visual stories.

The app suggests topics to explore, things to try, places to visit, and interesting events. New stories arrive every morning.

Instead of using stock imagery, each Dreambeans story is accompanied by Nano Banana 2-generated artwork that uses an illustrated style. For example, if Dreambeans recommends a hike, you might see yourself and a group of friends at that location.

	

Tapping on a story lets you see a longer description. In the same example, you’ll get trail details, specific places to stop, what to wear, and timing recommendations. Dreambeans will link to trail guide content on the web. There’s also an “Ask anything” chat experience to get more information.

You can leave feedback by tapping the heart or downvoting, while the chat interface allows you to provide more details. “Tune your feed” lets you tell Dreambeans what you “want more stories about” and what it should never show.

The name combines two ideas at the heart of the app. The “dream” is how the app works overnight to find meaning in the content overload across your connected apps. It then distills what it finds into “beans” – a fresh collection of stories brewed for you each morning.

In June, it was just available for Google AI Ultra subscribers, with Google expanding to AI Pro earlier this month. The setup process “requires up to a day to build your first set of stories.” 

It remains to be seen how Dreambeans will graduate from Google Labs. The experience it offers today is largely standalone, with Daily Brief in the Gemini app possibly benefiting from a more visual experience. 

Dreambeans is available on Android and iOS in the US.

title: MapQuest is now the No. 1 US app after bucking Trump’s ‘Lake America’ renaming
snippet: The once-dominant mapping app has surged to the top of Apple’s U.S. App Store after refusing to adopt Trump’s “Lake America” name, drawing more than half of its 2026 U.S. downloads in just six days.
fullText:
MapQuest’s unlikely comeback just got even bigger. On Tuesday, the “OG” mapping application (and one that many thought no longer existed!) became the No. 1 overall app on the U.S. App Store, up from No. 8 on Monday. 

The surge in new downloads was inspired by MapQuest’s refusal to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America,” after President Trump’s executive order directed the U.S. geographic naming service to adopt the new name amid his ongoing trade push.

After the August 27 order, MapQuest announced on X that it would not change the lake’s name, while both Google Maps and, later, Apple Maps, capitulated. As a result, MapQuest’s U.S. App Store ranking steadily climbed, as consumers downloaded the app to show their support for the company’s stance.

MapQuest’s rank climbed from No. 128 on August 28 to No. 92 the following day, and then hit No. 3 this Monday, August 31, when it was also No. 1 in the Navigation category. By Tuesday of this week, MapQuest had reached the No. 1 spot across both apps and games on the U.S. App Store.

Since the executive order was issued, the app has been downloaded an estimated 632,000 times in the U.S., according to data from market intelligence provider Sensor Tower. Reached for comment, MapQuest said the app had actually seen over 1.5 million installs across the U.S. and Canada combined.

MapQuest also said many of these new users aren’t just casual downloaders; they’re actively engaging with the app.

“What’s been incredible is that people aren’t just installing our app — they care enough to communicate directly with us — making feature requests and submitting bug reports on social, and in our app reviews,” MapQuest GM Doug Berger told TechCrunch via email. “Our small team has been working around the clock to build features people are asking for. We are aiming for everyone to have a great experience with the app,” he said.

The surge has come quickly for the company. More than half of MapQuest’s year-to-date U.S. downloads —56% — have occurred from August 27 through September 1, Sensor Tower’s estimates show. During this time period, the app’s U.S. downloads increased by 123% day-over-day and were up more than 50 times compared to the same period last year, its data indicates.

Part of what made MapQuest’s stance resonate with consumers was its contrast with its much larger Big Tech rivals. 

Google last week explained its decision to rename the lake, saying that it updates names to reflect changes in official government sources such as the Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) in the U.S. Apple didn’t provide a comment, but likely follows the same guidelines.

As a much smaller player, MapQuest has more freedom to take a stand and buck the typical conventions. 

ScreenshotImage Credits:MapQuest

This isn’t the first time it’s done so, either. It still calls the Gulf of Mexico by its original name, instead of Gulf of America. It even released a fun online tool that lets you jokingly rename Lake Ontario to whatever you want it to be, then share the results on social media.

Though it was once the original mapping application, MapQuest ceded its crown to Google Maps over the years. It’s now owned by the internet advertising company System1, which acquired the property from Verizon in 2019. The telco had bought MapQuest’s initial acquirer, AOL, in 2015.

title: Acer Shows Off a Transformer-ish Concept for a Windows Gaming Handheld
snippet: If it’s going to do double duty as a computer, it might as well have a keyboard, right?
fullText:
Project DualPlay MiniAcer/CNET

While we tend to think of Windows gaming handhelds as primarily gaming devices, they really have more in common with ultralight laptops: They run Windows, have a built-in screen and perform like them thanks to mobile processors with integrated graphics. And though some people have always used them as a primary computer, today’s high prices for both handhelds and traditional computers make handhelds seem like an even more attractive general-purpose option for gamers. 

But if you want to play a game with a keyboard and mouse, much less nongaming uses, you frequently experience the cumbersome process of connecting to the input devices or being restricted to wherever you’ve got a dock set up.

Project DualPlay MiniTara Brown/CNET

Acer’s Project DualPlay Mini concept takes a Transformers-like approach to making a handheld more suitable for general computing and KBM gaming: It’s a clamshell laptop design with the speakers on either side of the display, but the 8-inch screen flips up, and the grips are on the back of the speakers, so it turns into a traditional handheld when closed. 

You’d still have to connect a mouse, but the built-in keyboard remedies the most awkward design issue. As with any of these devices, you can connect to an external monitor as well as other peripherals as well.

The closest I’ve seen to a multipurpose design in a Windows gaming handheld is Lenovo’s Legion Go series (not the Legion Go Fold, though). But “close” in this case just comes down to a built-in kickstand that makes it a little easier to use on a desktop.

Predator Atlas 7

There aren’t any specs for it — it’s not a real product, at least at the moment — but Acer says it will use the same Intel G3 chips as in its Predator Atlas 8, announced at Computex 2026 in May and slated to ship later this month for an as-yet-unannounced price. The company has followed that with another launch this week for the Predator Atlas 7, a slightly smaller, lighter — and presumably cheaper — 7-inch model. It’s expected to ship around October or later in 2026.

title: Apple Maps still shows Lake Ontario as Google Maps changes name
snippet: The latest development in the trade war Trump started with Canada is an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America. Google Maps has updated the name, though what you see depends on which country you are in, with only US users seeing Lake America. Apple Maps has so far stuck to the real name … more…
fullText:
The latest development in the trade war Trump started with Canada is an executive order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America. Google Maps has updated the name, though what you see depends on which country you are in, with only US users seeing Lake America. Apple Maps has so far stuck to the real name … 

Lake Ontario is this year’s rerun of the Gulf of Mexico. Trump last year signed an executive order stating that the latter would be renamed to Gulf of America, and has now signed another saying that the smallest of the Great Lakes will be renamed Lake America.

Canada and most of the rest of the world has responded with amusement and mockery. Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a new billboard on the shoreline of the lake reading “Lake Ontario. Now and always.”

Google Maps has updated its naming, with the label depending on where you are based:

US users: Lake America

Canadian users: Lake Ontario

Rest of the world: Lake Ontario (Lake America)

This mirrors the approach the company took with the Gulf of Mexico. Associated Press cites a Google blog post stating that its policy is to use the names assigned by the U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS).

So far, however, Apple Maps has stuck to Lake Ontario, including for US users. Whether it too will compromise as it did for the Gulf of Mexico remains to be seen. The company normally tries to avoid political flak, and has often taken the decision to appease the Trump administration, but with a new CEO, this may or may not change.

title: Google Home update restores support for older Chromecast streamers, Home Mini
snippet: A rogue Google Home update earlier this year partially broke support for some older Chromecast streamers and other devices, but the latest update has restored it. more…
fullText:
A rogue Google Home update earlier this year partially broke support for some older Chromecast streamers and other devices, but the latest update has restored it. 

If you’re still using one of the original Chromecast streaming dongles over a decade later, first of all, kudos to you. While Google has technically dropped software support for its original 2013 streamer, the company continues to provide updates and support for other models. 

Back in May, it seemed as though the end had come for that first-gen device as support faltered in the Home app, but a fix arrived later on. It didn’t take long for further issues to appear, though. There was another wave of reports in late July, affecting not only the first-gen Chromecast, but also the 2015 model and Google Home Mini. The issue was primarily affecting setup, but also functionality to some extent, and mostly on the Android version of the Google Home app.

Google says this should be fixed as of Google Home v4.26 which is available now.

	

In a comment shared across several Reddit threads, Google explains:

We’ve resolved an issue that was impacting the ability to set up some older Chromecast and Google Home devices. If you haven’t already, factory reset their speaker or update your Google Home app to version 4.26 and try again…

You can download Google Home v4.26 via the Play Store, but you likely already have it installed.

title: Apple reportedly considered launching a new Apple Pencil for iPhone Ultra
snippet: Apple’s first foldable iPhone should be making its debut in just over a week. In the development process, Apple was reportedly mulling the idea of launching a new Apple Pencil to use alongside the iPhone Ultra – though it probably won’t make it to market. more…
fullText:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone should be making its debut in just over a week. In the development process, Apple was reportedly mulling the idea of launching a new Apple Pencil to use alongside the iPhone Ultra – though it probably won’t make it to market.

This news comes from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who wants to make it very clear that this pencil probably won’t be announced next month. That said, he does detail exactly how it would’ve looked and worked.

It wouldn’t have been the same as Apple Pencils that currently exist for the iPad lineup. It was “stubbier,” to align with the shorter height of the iPhone Ultra. However, similar to Apple Pencils on the iPad, it would’ve magnetically attached to the side for storage and charging.

He notes that it would’ve been awkward to hold while you were using the iPhone Ultra, since it’d stick on the side, versus the iPad where it sticks at the top when you’re in landscape.

He also notes that it likely would’ve made “unsightly marks” on the much more delicate inside screen of the iPhone Ultra.

Ultimately, he reckons that Apple probably isn’t launching this to not conflict with Steve Jobs’ position when launching the original iPhone: “Who wants a stylus?”

I’d still say an Apple Pencil on iPhone Ultra would be rather useful, but it sounds like we won’t have one – at least for the time being.

title: CarPlay keeps getting better with three recent exciting app updates
snippet: CarPlay is about to get even better with iOS 27 in September. New features including a dedicated Siri app and Siri AI will upgrade Apple’s car infotainment system for iPhone users. Even before the big iPhone software update officially launches, CarPlay in August has improved for everyone with three big app releases. more…
fullText:
CarPlay is about to get even better with iOS 27 in September. New features including a dedicated Siri app and Siri AI will upgrade Apple’s car infotainment system for iPhone users.

Even before the big iPhone software update officially launches, CarPlay in August has improved for everyone with three big app releases.

MLB iPhone app enhances CarPlay experience

First, MLB upgraded their iPhone app in the middle of the baseball season to improve the CarPlay experience.

Fans can browse live and upcoming games, select a matchup, and choose their preferred team’s radio feed. 

CarPlay also now shows baseball scores and key game details while the broadcast plays, with the app’s hide-scores setting respected for anyone avoiding spoilers.

Next, Meta AI for iPhone now works with CarPlay — with a catch.

The Meta AI app joins three other third-party chatbot apps that work with CarPlay: ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Grok.

However, Meta AI on CarPlay appears to be in limited testing for now.

Still, this shows the key benefit of CarPlay: integrating existing iPhone apps with your vehicle. You just can’t expect this amount of AI chatbot choice from built-in infotainment systems.

CarPlay adds a major weather app

The third big CarPlay app in August is Storm Radar from The Weather Channel.

Storm Radar for CarPlay includes a map of your location. You can toggle between satellite view and the default map background. Data layers include radar, clouds, and precipitation. 

Navigation is also a core part of the CarPlay app. Storm Radar displays your current weather conditions alongside the ETA and weather conditions expected at your destination.

The Weather Channel adds that CarPlay support includes “automatic rerouting and weather alerts along your route that refresh as you drive.”

More CarPlay upgrades

Looking ahead, Apple will upgrade CarPlay for everyone with the upcoming iOS 27 iPhone update. Installing the iPhone software update or upgrading to a new iPhone running iOS 27 when it comes out will automatically add new features to CarPlay.

In the meantime, Volvo has upgraded three SUVs with Spatial Audio through CarPlay for Apple Music and Apple Podcasts. This brings Dolby Atmos sound support to drivers. Earlier this year, Pioneer released an aftermarket head unit that similarly drives Dolby Atmos and Spatial Audio through CarPlay.

title: Google spared from ad-business breakup, but judge orders changes to how it operates
snippet: Google has dodged an effort to break up its ad business, but a judge said Wednesday that the company will need to adjust its business to benefit competitors.
fullText:
The Justice Department has spent years attempting to break up Google’s gargantuan advertising business across two separate antitrust lawsuits: one filed in 2020 focused on Google’s dominance in search, and a second filed in 2023 that specifically targeted Google’s ad-technology business. Both cases argued that the search giant’s grip on the digital ad economy represents an illegal monopoly.

Courts have largely sided with the government in both cases. In 2024, a court determined that Google’s search business, including its exceedingly lucrative search-ad operation, was an illegal monopoly, claiming that the tech giant had “exercised its monopoly power” to dominate the search industry and search ads. Last April, a second court case — this one focused specifically on Google’s ad-tech business — also came to the same conclusion.

Following the 2024 ruling, Justice Department officials suggested a variety of ways Google’s search business could be broken up, including divesting its Chrome browser and Android operating system. But in September 2025, the judge overseeing that case, Amit Mehta, rejected those divestiture requests, ruling that Google could keep both Chrome and Android. He did order the company to end exclusive default-placement deals and share certain search data with competitors (remedies that Google is currently appealing).

That same pattern held this week. In a ruling handed down on Wednesday, federal judge Leonie M. Brinkema of the Eastern District of Virginia, who oversaw the ad-tech case, said that Google would be able to keep its advertising business. Instead of selling it, the search giant will instead be required to adjust its business practices to favor competitors, Brinkema said. The New York Times notes that the judge’s ruling “did not provide specifics” as to how Google should go about doing that.

Brinkema’s full written ruling will remain under seal for 14 days to allow those involved to issue necessary redactions. Her finding that Google had acted illegally in maintaining its ad-tech business dates back to April of last year; this week’s decision addressed only the remedy.

Unsurprisingly, Google framed the outcome as a win. Lee-Anne Mulholland, Google’s vice president for regulatory affairs, told TechCrunch: “We’re very pleased the Court rejected the DOJ’s proposal to break apart tools that help small businesses reach new customers and grow.”

The online advertising ecosystem is notoriously opaque and byzantine and, for most people unfamiliar with its complexities, difficult to grasp. Much of the government’s ad-tech case against Google revolved around the company’s tactics to ensure that its search engine was the default engine in devices across the world, which in turn helped its ad business dominate as well.

To do this, Google used exclusive agreements with device manufacturers, which made it the default search engine across huge swaths of the mobile phone market, the government has argued. Google also entered into revenue sharing agreements with mobile carriers — deals where carriers earned a cut of ad revenue in exchange for keeping Google as the default — that further cemented its position as the de facto search engine across phone markets.

title: Belkin just released four Android Find Hub trackers; one is a full wallet
snippet: More companies are getting on board with trackers that work with the Android Find Hub network, and Belkin is the latest with four different designs. more…
fullText:
More companies are getting on board with trackers that work with the Android Find Hub network, and Belkin is the latest with four different designs.

Trackers come in all shapes and sizes, as long as the size is small and the shape is circular or rectangular. Belkin is mostly sticking to that unwritten rule with several entries in its new SureFind lineup starting at $15.

The smallest and most familiar tracker is the SureFind Spot. It’s the cheapest of the bunch at $15, and it looks a lot like an Apple AirTag, with a keyring included. The SureFind Loop Cable Tag is similar, but the fabric loop doubles as a spare USB-C cable. It’s a little more robust than the Spot, but it fits a similar profile for bags or everyday carry items that don’t require a compact solution. It also charges via USB-C, so it doesn’t need a coin-cell replacement every so often. The SureFind Loop Cable Tag will cost $24.99.

Belkin also released a card-shaped Android Find Hub tracker. Just like other tracker cards, the SureFind Card fits into most wallets and takes up no more space than a credit card. Its ultra-thin profile opens it up to other hiding places, as well. Belkin’s tracker card is IP68 for water and dust-resistance, too. It’s priced in the same area as the Loop Tag, at $26.99.

	

Of all the trackers Belkin announced, the last one is the most unique. We’ve seen the form-factor before, but it’s a welcome one. You could opt to slide a tracking card into your wallet, or you could skip that step and buy a wallet that connects to Google’s Find Hub network.

Belkin’s SureFind Wallet Stand shows up in your Find Hub app like every other tracker, but it can’t be easily removed if someone were to take it. It doubles as a magnetic phone stand and comes in a thin compact profile that allows you to store a couple of cards. It’s the most expensive tracker Belkin released at IFA, coming in at $39.99.

Belkin says the SureFind Spot, Loop Cable Tag, and Card will be available starting this month from Amazon and its online store. The SureFind Wallet Stand will go on sale at the beginning of October.

title: As a relatively new Apple Vision Pro user, this is my favorite way to use it
snippet: Apple Vision Pro is one of Apple’s most interesting hardware releases yet. It’s technically very impressive, yet it seems almost certain that this form factor won’t last – and is instead just a temporary platform to introduce visionOS to the world before we eventually get glasses. I did buy one late last year, and while I haven’t been a major user of it, there is one use case that genuinely makes it enjoyable. more…
fullText:
Apple Vision Pro is one of Apple’s most interesting hardware releases yet. It’s technically very impressive, yet it seems almost certain that this form factor won’t last – and is instead just a temporary platform to introduce visionOS to the world before we eventually get glasses.

I did buy one late last year, and while I haven’t been a major user of it, there is one use case that genuinely makes it enjoyable.

When Vision Pro launched, the potential seemed endless. It’d be the headset to end all screens. Mac Virtual Display seemed awesome, and so did the idea of spatial FaceTime – even if Persona’s were a bit jarring at launch.

Then, once the honeymoon phase wore off, people started to realize the headset was quite heavy, making it hard to use for a long period of time. This meant that a lot of people begun selling their Vision Pros, allowing you to pick up a used one for a substantially discounted price.

They average around $1500 right now – a much smaller pill to swallow than the new $3699 starting price point.

If Vision Pro excels at one thing, it’s content consumption. The App Store might not be the most compelling in most regards, though you do have most streaming apps, including Disney+, HBO Max, and even YouTube now. Netflix is the biggest outlier. Of course, you also have Apple TV.

The best way to enjoy Vision Pro

Outgoing Apple CEO Tim Cook shared his favorite way to use Vision Pro back in January 2025, and recently referenced it again last month in an interview at the season 4 premiere of Ted Lasso:

Funnily enough, Cook was asked if he plans to watch Ted Lasso season 4 on Apple Vision Pro. That was reportedly how he watched season 3. “Oh yes, of course, and watch it lying down on Vision Pro, there’s nothing quite like that.”

I can’t say I exclusively watch shows and movies in Vision Pro. It’s a lot to commit to sometimes, since multitasking on Vision Pro is sometimes a struggle with its poor software keyboard.

When I am watching a show or movie in Vision Pro, though, I am exclusively doing it using the Tim Cook method: lying down and staring upwards. It completely erases the weight concern, and is a pretty relaxing experience if you have the time to commit to it.

Vision Pro is a rather expensive product to only use to occasionally watch television, at least at its MSRP. With how much they’ve depreciated though, I think buying one just to use as a bedtime face TV isn’t necessarily an awful idea. It’s an enjoyable experience, especially when you’re watching in 3D.

title: Google will not have to sell AdX business, but it will have to make changes
snippet: Following a prior court battle, a judge has now ruled that Google won’t have to sell off its AdX (ad exchange) business after all, and will instead have to make some undisclosed behavioral changes. more…
fullText:
Following a prior court battle, a judge has now ruled that Google won’t have to sell off its AdX (ad exchange) business after all, and will instead have to make some undisclosed behavioral changes.

As reported by Bloomberg and The New York Times, Google will not have to sell off its AdX business. Judge Leonie Brinkema rejected the DOJ’s move to force the sale of that business which would have also make the auction logic behind ad placements public information. 

While Google won’t have to sell off the business or reveal auction logic, the Judge did propose “behavioral changes.”

We’ll know more in 14 days when the decision is unsealed, as both Google and the DOJ will be able to use that time to make any needed redactions. 

	

Still, it’s a major victory on Google’s part. The 2025 ruling still finds Google guilty of breaking the law to protect a monopoly on advertising, but as ArsTechnica points out, the sale of AdX could have made an impact in the rest of Google’s advertising business even if the ad exchange in particular isn’t the biggest part of that business.
